bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第034卷

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 34.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 34.

sentences.zh: 【漢紀二十六】起柔兆執徐，盡著雍敦牂，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Han Annals 26] From Rouzhao Zhixu through Zhuoyong Dunzhang; three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Han Annals 26] From Rouzhao Zhixu through Zhuoyong Dunzhang—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，有星孛於牽牛。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, a broom star appeared in the Ox constellation.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, a comet appeared in the Ox constellation.

sentences.zh: 丁、傅宗族驕奢，皆嫉傅喜之恭儉。

translations.literal: The Ding and Fu clans were arrogant and extravagant; all envied Fu Xi's modesty and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: The Ding and Fu clans were arrogant and extravagant, and all envied Fu Xi's modesty and restraint.

sentences.zh: 又，傅太后欲求稱尊號，與成帝母齊尊；

translations.literal: Moreover, Empress Dowager Fu wished to take an honored title, equal in honor to Emperor Cheng's mother;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Empress Dowager Fu wished to take an honored title equal to Emperor Cheng's mother;

sentences.zh: 喜與孔光、師丹共執以為不可。

translations.literal: Fu Xi, together with Kong Guang and Shi Dan, jointly held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi, together with Kong Guang and Shi Dan, firmly held that it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 上重違大臣正議，又內迫傅太后，依違者連歲。

translations.literal: The emperor weighed going against the ministers' upright counsel, yet was inwardly pressed by Empress Dowager Fu; he wavered for years on end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor weighed defying his ministers' upright counsel, yet was pressed from within by Empress Dowager Fu; he wavered year after year.

sentences.zh: 傅太后大怒，上不得已，先免師丹以感動喜。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Fu was greatly angry; the emperor had no choice and first removed Shi Dan to move Fu Xi emotionally.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Fu was furious; the emperor had no choice and first removed Shi Dan, hoping to move Fu Xi.

sentences.zh: 喜終不順。

translations.literal: Fu Xi in the end would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi would not yield in the end.

sentences.zh: 朱博與孔鄉侯傅晏連結，共謀成尊號事，數燕見，奏封事，毀短喜及孔光。

translations.literal: Zhu Bo allied with Marquis of Kongxiang Fu Yan, together plotting to accomplish the honored-title affair; he had frequent informal audiences, submitted sealed memorials, and defamed Fu Xi and Kong Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bo allied with Marquis of Kongxiang Fu Yan to accomplish the honored-title affair; he had frequent informal audiences, submitted sealed memorials, and defamed Fu Xi and Kong Guang.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，上遂策免喜，以侯就第。

translations.literal: On dingchou, the emperor then removed Fu Xi by patent and sent him to his marquisate residence as a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, the emperor removed Fu Xi by patent and sent him to his marquisate residence.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫官既罷，議者多以為古今異制，漢自天子之號下至佐史，皆不同於古，而獨改三公，職事難分明，無益於治亂。

translations.literal: Since the office of Censor-in-Chief had been abolished, many deliberators held that ancient and modern systems differ; from the Son of Heaven's title down to clerk and scribe, Han differed from antiquity in all, yet only the Three Ducal Ministers were changed—their duties hard to distinguish clearly, of no benefit to order or disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Censor-in-Chief had been abolished, many held that ancient and modern systems differed: from the Son of Heaven's title down to clerk and scribe, Han differed from antiquity throughout, yet only the Three Ducal Ministers were changed—duties hard to distinguish, with no benefit to order or disorder.

sentences.zh: 於是朱博奏言：「故事：選郡國守相高第為中二千石，選中二千石為御史大夫，任職者為丞相；

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhu Bo memorialized, saying: "By precedent: select commandery and kingdom governors and administrators of high grade as rank-2000-shi; select rank-2000-shi as Censor-in-Chief; the one who takes office becomes Chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhu Bo memorialized: "By precedent, commandery and kingdom governors and administrators of high grade were made rank-2000-shi; rank-2000-shi were made Censor-in-Chief; the incumbent became Chancellor;

sentences.zh: 位次有序，所以尊聖德，重國相也。

translations.literal: ranks ordered in sequence, thereby to honor sagely virtue and weight the state's premier.
translations.idiomatic: ranks were ordered in sequence, thereby honoring sagely virtue and weighting the state's premier.

sentences.zh: 今中二千石未更御史大夫而為丞相，權輕，非所以重國政也。

translations.literal: Now rank-2000-shi who have not passed through Censor-in-Chief become Chancellor—authority is light; this is not how to weight state government.
translations.idiomatic: Now rank-2000-shi who have not served as Censor-in-Chief become Chancellor—authority is too light; this is not how to weight state government.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為大司空官可罷，復置御史大夫，遵奉舊制。

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish and holds that the Grand Minister of Works office may be abolished, the Censor-in-Chief restored, following the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that the Grand Minister of Works may be abolished and the Censor-in-Chief restored, following the old system.

sentences.zh: 臣願盡力以御史大夫為百僚率！

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to exhaust his strength as Censor-in-Chief, leader of the hundred officials!
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes to give his utmost as Censor-in-Chief, leader of the hundred officials!

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed this.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊午，更拜博為御史大夫。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on wuwu, Bo was reappointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on wuwu, Zhu Bo was reappointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 又以丁太后兄陽安侯明為大司馬、衛將軍，置官屬；

translations.literal: Ding the Empress Dowager's elder brother, Marquis of Yang'an Ming, was also made Grand Marshal and Defender General, with staff appointed;
translations.idiomatic: Ding the Empress Dowager's elder brother, Marquis of Yang'an Ming, was also made Grand Marshal and Defender General, with a staff appointed;

sentences.zh: 大司馬冠號如故事。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal's cap and title followed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal's cap and title followed precedent.

sentences.zh: 傅太后又自詔丞相、御史大夫曰：「高武侯喜附下罔上，與故大司空丹同心背畔，放命圮族，不宜奉朝請，其遣就國。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Fu herself edicted the Chancellor and Censor-in-Chief, saying: "Marquis of Gaowu Fu Xi fawned on subordinates and deceived superiors; with the former Grand Minister of Works Dan he shared one heart in rebellion, reckless mandate destroying the clan—he ought not attend court audiences; send him to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Fu herself edicted the Chancellor and Censor-in-Chief: "Marquis of Gaowu Fu Xi fawned on subordinates and deceived his superiors; with the former Grand Minister of Works Shi Dan he conspired in rebellion and reckless defiance that ruined the clan. He ought not attend court—send him to his state.

sentences.zh: 丞相孔光，自先帝時議繼嗣，有持異之隙，又重忤傅太后指。

translations.literal: Chancellor Kong Guang, from when the late emperor deliberated the succession, had a rift of holding divergent views, and again deeply offended Empress Dowager Fu's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Kong Guang, from when the late emperor deliberated the succession, had a rift over holding divergent views, and again deeply offended Empress Dowager Fu.

sentences.zh: 由是傅氏在位者與朱博為表裡，共毀譖光。

translations.literal: Thereupon those of the Fu clan in office and Zhu Bo were outer and inner layers, jointly slandering Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Fu clan in office and Zhu Bo worked hand in glove, jointly slandering Kong Guang.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，策免光為庶人。

translations.literal: On yihai, Guang was removed by patent to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Kong Guang was removed by patent to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 以御史大夫朱博為丞相，封陽鄉侯；

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhu Bo was made Chancellor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangxiang;
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zhu Bo was made Chancellor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangxiang;

sentences.zh: 少府趙玄為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Privy Treasurer Zhao Xuan was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Treasurer Zhao Xuan was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 臨延登受策，有大聲如鐘鳴，殿中郎吏陛者皆聞焉。

translations.literal: As he was about to ascend and receive the patent, a great sound like a bell ringing—all the gentlemen-attendants and clerks on the palace steps heard it.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhu Bo was about to ascend and receive his patent of appointment, a great sound like a bell rang out, and all the gentlemen-attendants and clerks on the palace steps heard it.

sentences.zh: 上以問黃門侍郎蜀郡揚雄及李尋。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Yellow Gate Gentleman-attendant Yang Xiong of Shu Commandery and Li Xun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Yellow Gate Gentleman-attendant Yang Xiong of Shu Commandery and Li Xun.

sentences.zh: 尋對曰：「此《洪範》所謂鼓妖者也。

translations.literal: Xun replied, saying: "This is what the Hong Fan calls a drum demon.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun replied: "This is what the Hong Fan calls a drum demon.

sentences.zh: 師法，以為人君不聰，為眾所惑，空名得進，則有聲無形，不知所從生。

translations.literal: By masterly method, it is held that when the ruler is not perspicacious, is deluded by the multitude, and empty names advance, then there is sound without form, not knowing whence it is born.
translations.idiomatic: By masterly interpretation, when the ruler is not perspicacious and is deluded by the multitude, and empty names advance, there is sound without form, with no knowing whence it arises.

sentences.zh: 其《傳》曰：『歲、月、日之中，則正卿受之。

translations.literal: Its Commentary says: 'Within the year, month, and day, the chief minister receives it.
translations.idiomatic: Its Commentary says, 'Within the year, month, and day, the chief minister receives it.

sentences.zh: 』今以四月日加辰、巳有異，是為中焉。

translations.literal: ' Now on a day in the fourth month adding chen and si there was an anomaly—this is being within.
translations.idiomatic: ' Now on a day in the fourth month, at chen and si hours, there was an anomaly—this counts as being within.

sentences.zh: 正卿，謂執政大臣也。

translations.literal: Chief minister means the minister holding government.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister means the minister holding power.

sentences.zh: 宜退丞相、御史，以應天變。

translations.literal: The Chancellor and Censor ought to retire to respond to Heaven's change.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor and Censor ought to retire to answer Heaven's omen.

sentences.zh: 然雖不退，不出期年，其人自蒙其咎。

translations.literal: Yet even if they do not retire, within a year the man himself will bear the blame.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even if they do not retire, within a year the man himself will bear the blame.

sentences.zh: 」揚雄亦以為：「鼓妖，聽失之象也。

translations.literal: " Yang Xiong also held: "The drum demon is a sign of failure in hearing.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Xiong also held: "The drum demon is a sign of failure in hearing.

sentences.zh: 朱博為人強毅，多權謀，宜將不宜相，恐有凶惡亟疾之怒。

translations.literal: Zhu Bo by nature is forceful and resolute, full of power-plots—fit for general, unfit for premier; I fear sudden fierce angry harm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bo is forceful and resolute, full of stratagems—fit for a general, unfit for chancellor; I fear sudden fierce harm born of wrath.

sentences.zh: 」上不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 朱博既為丞相，上遂用其議，下詔曰：「定陶共皇之號，不宜復稱定陶。

translations.literal: Zhu Bo having become Chancellor, the emperor then used his proposal and issued an edict, saying: "The title Lord Gong of Dingtao ought not again be called Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhu Bo became Chancellor, the emperor adopted his proposal and issued an edict: "The title Lord Gong of Dingtao ought not again be called Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 尊共皇太后曰帝太太后，稱永信宮；

translations.literal: Honor the late Lord Gong's empress dowager as Grand Imperial Empress Dowager, styled Everlasting Faith Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Honor the late Lord Gong's empress dowager as Grand Imperial Empress Dowager, with the style Everlasting Faith Palace;

sentences.zh: 共皇后曰帝太后，稱中安宮；

translations.literal: the late queen as Imperial Empress Dowager, styled Central Peace Palace;
translations.idiomatic: the late queen as Imperial Empress Dowager, with the style Central Peace Palace;

sentences.zh: 為共皇立寢廟於京師，比宣帝父悼皇考制度。

translations.literal: establish a resting temple for Lord Gong in the capital, matching Emperor Xuan's father the Lamented Emperor's system.
translations.idiomatic: establish a resting temple for Lord Gong in the capital, matching the system for Emperor Xuan's father, the Lamented Emperor.

sentences.zh: 」於是四太后各置少府、太僕，秩皆中二千石。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the four empress dowagers each had Privy Treasurer and Grand Coach Master appointed, all at rank full 2000-shi.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon each of the four empress dowagers was given a Privy Treasurer and Grand Coach Master at rank full 2000-shi.

sentences.zh: 傅太后既尊後。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Fu having been honored thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Once Empress Dowager Fu had been honored.

sentences.zh: 尤驕，與太皇太后語，至謂之「嫗」。

translations.literal: She was especially arrogant; speaking with the Grand Empress Dowager, she even called her "old woman."
translations.idiomatic: She grew especially arrogant; in speaking with the Grand Empress Dowager she even called her "old woman."

sentences.zh: 時丁、傅以一二年間暴興尤盛，為公卿列侯者甚眾。

translations.literal: At the time the Ding and Fu clans within a year or two had risen with sudden violence especially strong—many became dukes, ministers, and ranked marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year or two the Ding and Fu clans had risen with sudden violence; many held posts as dukes, ministers, and ranked marquises.

sentences.zh: 然帝不甚假以權勢，不如王氏在成帝世也。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor did not greatly lend them power and favor, not like the Wang clan in Emperor Cheng's age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor did not lend them much power or favor—not as the Wang clan had enjoyed in Emperor Cheng's reign.

sentences.zh: 丞相博、御史大夫玄奏言：「前高昌侯宏，首建尊號之議，而為關內侯師丹所劾奏，免為庶人。

translations.literal: Chancellor Bo and Censor-in-Chief Xuan memorialized, saying: "Formerly Marquis of Gaochang Hong first established the honored-title proposal, yet was impeached and memorialized against by Marquis within the Passes Shi Dan and removed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhu Bo and Censor-in-Chief Zhao Xuan memorialized: "Formerly Marquis of Gaochang Dong Hong first proposed the honored title, yet Marquis within the Passes Shi Dan impeached him and he was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 時天下衰粗，委政於丹，丹不深惟褒廣尊號之義，而妄稱說，抑貶尊號，虧損孝道，不忠莫大焉！

translations.literal: At the time the realm was coarse and declining, government was entrusted to Dan; Dan did not deeply consider the meaning of honoring and extending the honored title, but spoke rashly, suppressed and demeaned the honored title, damaged filial piety—no disloyalty greater!
translations.idiomatic: The realm was coarse and declining, and government was entrusted to Shi Dan; Dan did not deeply weigh the meaning of honoring and extending the honored title, but spoke rashly, suppressed and demeaned it, and damaged filial piety—no disloyalty could be greater!

sentences.zh: 陛下仁聖，昭然定尊號，宏以忠孝復封高昌侯；

translations.literal: Your Majesty is benevolent and sage, clearly establishing the honored title; Hong by loyalty and filial piety is again enfeoffed Marquis of Gaochang;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is benevolent and sage and has clearly established the honored title; Hong, through loyalty and filial piety, is again enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaochang;

sentences.zh: 丹惡逆暴著，雖蒙赦令，不宜有爵邑，請免為庶人。

translations.literal: Dan's wicked rebellion is glaring; though he received amnesty, he ought not hold rank and fief—request removal to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan's wicked rebellion stands glaring; though he received amnesty, he ought not hold rank and fief—we ask that he be reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「新都侯王莽前為大司馬，不廣尊尊之義，抑貶尊號，虧損孝道，當伏顯戮。

translations.literal: They also memorialized: "Marquis of Xindu Wang Mang, formerly as Grand Marshal, did not extend the meaning of honoring the honored, suppressed the honored title, damaged filial piety—ought to suffer manifest execution.
translations.idiomatic: They also memorialized: "Marquis of Xindu Wang Mang, formerly Grand Marshal, did not extend the meaning of honoring the honored, suppressed the honored title, and damaged filial piety—he ought to suffer public execution.

sentences.zh: 幸蒙赦令，不宜有爵土，請免為庶人。

translations.literal: Fortunately receiving amnesty, he ought not hold rank and land—request reduction to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately he received amnesty, but he ought not hold rank and land—we ask that he be reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「以莽與太皇太后有屬，勿免，遣就國。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Because Mang is kin to the Grand Empress Dowager, do not remove him—send him to his state.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "Because Wang Mang is kin to the Grand Empress Dowager, do not remove him—send him to his state.

sentences.zh: 」及平阿侯仁臧匿趙昭儀親屬，皆遣就國。

translations.literal: " And Marquis of Ping'e Ren, who concealed Consort Zhao Zhaoyi's kin, all were sent to their states.
translations.idiomatic: " Marquis of Ping'e Liu Ren, who had concealed Consort Zhao Zhaoyi's kin, was also sent to his state.

sentences.zh: 天下多冤王氏者。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm many held the Wang clan wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm many held that the Wang clan had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 諫大夫楊宣上封事言：「孝成皇帝深惟宗廟之重，稱述陛下至德以承天序，聖策深遠，恩德至厚。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Grandee Yang Xuan submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "Emperor Cheng deeply pondered the weight of the ancestral temple, praised Your Majesty's utmost virtue to continue Heaven's sequence—sage policy deep and far, grace and virtue utmost thick.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Grandee Yang Xuan submitted a sealed memorial: "Emperor Cheng deeply weighed the ancestral temple, praised Your Majesty's utmost virtue to continue Heaven's sequence—his sage policy was deep and far-reaching, his grace and virtue exceedingly great.

sentences.zh: 惟念先帝之意，豈不欲以陛下自代，奉承東宮哉！

translations.literal: Pondering the late emperor's intent—did he not wish to have Your Majesty replace him and attend the Eastern Palace!
translations.idiomatic: Reflect on the late emperor's intent—did he not wish to have Your Majesty succeed him and attend the Eastern Palace!

sentences.zh: 太皇太后春秋七十，數更憂傷，敕令親屬引領以避丁、傅，行道之人為之隕涕，況於陛下！

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager is seventy years of age, has suffered grief again and again; her edict has kin stretch their necks to avoid Ding and Fu—the passers-by shed tears for it, how much more Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager is seventy and has suffered grief again and again; her edict has her kin stretch their necks to avoid the Ding and Fu clans—passers-by shed tears at the sight, how much more should Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 時登高遠望，獨不慚於延陵乎！

translations.literal: At times climbing high and gazing far—are you alone not ashamed before Yanling!
translations.idiomatic: When you climb high and gaze far, are you alone not ashamed before Yanling!

sentences.zh: 」帝深感其言，復封成都侯商中子邑為成都侯。

translations.literal: " The emperor was deeply moved by these words and re-enfeoffed Shang's middle son Yi of Marquis of Chengdu as Marquis of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply moved and re-enfeoffed the middle son Yi of Marquis of Chengdu Wang Shang as Marquis of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 朱博又奏言：「漢家故事，置部刺史，秩卑而賞厚，鹹勸功樂進。

translations.literal: Zhu Bo again memorialized, saying: "Han house precedent placed regional inspectors—rank low yet rewards thick; all urged merit and delighted in advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bo again memorialized: "By Han precedent, regional inspectors were appointed—rank low yet rewards generous, so all urged merit and delighted in advancement.

sentences.zh: 前罷刺史，更置州牧，秩真二千石，位次九卿；

translations.literal: Formerly inspectors were abolished and regional governors set instead, salary true 2000-shi, rank after the Nine Ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors were abolished and regional governors appointed instead, at salary true 2000-shi and rank after the Nine Ministers;

sentences.zh: 九卿缺，以高第補；

translations.literal: when the Nine Ministers lacked, filled by high grade;
translations.idiomatic: when the Nine Ministers had vacancies, they were filled from high-grade men;

sentences.zh: 其中材則苟自守而已。

translations.literal: those of middling talent then merely kept themselves guarded.
translations.idiomatic: men of middling talent merely kept themselves intact.

sentences.zh: 恐功效陵夷，奸軌不禁。

translations.literal: I fear achievements would decline and villainy go unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: I fear achievements would decline and villainy go unchecked.

sentences.zh: 臣請罷州牧，置刺史如故。

translations.literal: Your servant requests abolishing regional governors and restoring inspectors as before.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant asks that regional governors be abolished and inspectors restored as before.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed this.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚申，帝太后丁氏崩，詔歸葬定陶共皇之園，發陳留、濟陰近郡國五萬人穿復土。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengshen, Imperial Empress Dowager Ding died; an edict ordered return burial to Lord Gong of Dingtao's park; fifty thousand men from Chenliu and Jiyin and nearby commanderies and kingdoms were mobilized to dig and mound earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengshen, Imperial Empress Dowager Ding died; an edict ordered burial in Lord Gong of Dingtao's park and mobilized fifty thousand men from Chenliu, Jiyin, and nearby commanderies and kingdoms to dig and mound the tomb.

sentences.zh: 初，成帝時，齊人甘忠可詐造《天官歷》、《包元太平經》十二卷，言漢家逢天地之大終，當更受命於天，以教渤海夏賀良等。

translations.literal: Initially, in Emperor Cheng's time, Gan Zhongke of Qi fraudulently made the Heavenly Offices Calendar and twelve scrolls of the Bao yuan Taiping Classic, saying the Han house met Heaven and Earth's great end and ought again to receive mandate from Heaven, to teach Bohai's Xia Heliang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Emperor Cheng's reign, Gan Zhongke of Qi forged the Heavenly Offices Calendar and twelve scrolls of the Bao yuan Taiping Classic, claiming the Han house had reached Heaven and Earth's great end and must receive a new mandate from Heaven, which he taught to Xia Heliang of Bohai and others.

sentences.zh: 中壘校尉劉向奏忠可假鬼神，罔上惑眾；

translations.literal: Central Stackade Commandant Liu Xiang memorialized that Zhongke feigned ghosts and spirits, deceived superiors and deluded the multitude;
translations.idiomatic: Central Stackade Commandant Liu Xiang memorialized that Zhongke feigned ghosts and spirits to deceive his superiors and delude the multitude;

sentences.zh: 下獄，治服；

translations.literal: he was sent to prison and pleaded guilty;
translations.idiomatic: he was imprisoned and pleaded guilty;

sentences.zh: 未斷，病死。

translations.literal: before sentence was passed, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: before sentence was passed, he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 賀良等復私以相教。

translations.literal: Heliang and others again privately taught one another.
translations.idiomatic: Heliang and others again taught one another in private.

sentences.zh: 上即位，司隸校尉解光、騎都尉李尋白賀良等，皆待詔黃門。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Metropolitan Commandant Jie Guang and Commandant of Cavalry Li Xun reported Heliang and others; all awaited edict at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Metropolitan Commandant Jie Guang and Commandant of Cavalry Li Xun reported Heliang and others, and all were kept awaiting edict at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 數召見，陳說「漢歷中衰，當更受命。

translations.literal: They were summoned repeatedly and stated: "The Han calendar is in mid-decline; it ought to renew its mandate.
translations.idiomatic: They were summoned repeatedly and declared: "The Han calendar is in mid-decline and must renew its mandate.

sentences.zh: 成帝不應天命，故絕嗣。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng did not respond to Heaven's mandate, therefore no heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng did not answer Heaven's mandate, and therefore left no heir.

sentences.zh: 今陛下久疾，變異屢數，天所以譴告人也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's long illness and anomalies repeatedly numbered—this is Heaven's way of admonishing men.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's long illness and repeated anomalies are Heaven's way of admonishing mankind.

sentences.zh: 宜急改元易號，乃得延年益壽，皇子生，災異息矣。

translations.literal: You ought urgently to change the era name and alter the title, then obtain extended years and increased life, a prince born, and disasters and anomalies stilled.
translations.idiomatic: You ought urgently to change the era name and alter your title—then you will gain long life, a prince will be born, and disasters and anomalies will cease.

sentences.zh: 得道不得行，咎殃且無不有，洪水將出，災火且起，滌蕩民人。

translations.literal: Obtaining the Way yet not acting—blame and calamity will all come; floods will issue, disaster fire will rise, washing and sweeping the people.
translations.idiomatic: If you obtain the Way yet do not act, blame and calamity will follow without fail; floods will rise, disaster fire will break out, and the people will be swept away.

sentences.zh: 」上久寢疾，冀其有益，遂從賀良等議，詔大赦天下，以建平二年為太初元年，號曰「陳聖劉太平皇帝」，漏刻以百二十為度。

translations.literal: " The emperor had long been ill and hoped for benefit; he thereupon followed Heliang's proposal, edicting a general amnesty throughout the realm, making Jianping year 2 into Taichu year 1, with the title "Chen Sheng Liu Taiping Emperor," and clepsydra graduations set at one hundred twenty.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor had long been ill and hoped for benefit; he followed Heliang's proposal, proclaimed a general amnesty, made Jianping year 2 into Taichu year 1, took the title "Chen Sheng Liu Taiping Emperor," and set the clepsydra graduations at one hundred twenty.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以渭城西北原上永陵亭部為初陵，勿徙郡國民。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Yongling pavilion district on the northwest plateau of Weicheng was made Chuling; commandery and kingdom people were not to be relocated.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the Yongling pavilion district on the northwest plateau of Weicheng was made Chuling, and commandery and kingdom people were not to be relocated.

sentences.zh: 上既改號月餘，寢疾自若。

translations.literal: The emperor, having changed his title for more than a month, was ill as before.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month after changing his title, the emperor's illness was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 夏賀良等復欲妄變政事，大臣爭以為不可許。

translations.literal: Xia Heliang and others again wished rashly to alter government affairs; the great ministers contended that it must not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Heliang and others again wished rashly to alter government affairs, and the ministers contended that this must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 賀良等奏言：「大臣皆不知天命，宜退丞相、御史，以解光、李尋輔政。

translations.literal: Heliang and others memorialized, saying: "The great ministers all do not know Heaven's mandate—the Chancellor and Censor ought to retire, and Jie Guang and Li Xun ought to assist government.
translations.idiomatic: Heliang and others memorialized: "The ministers do not know Heaven's mandate—the Chancellor and Censor ought to retire, and Jie Guang and Li Xun ought to assist government.

sentences.zh: 」上以其言無驗，八月，詔曰：「待詔賀良等建言改元易號，增益漏刻，可以永安國家。

translations.literal: " The emperor, their words unverified, in the eighth month issued an edict, saying: "Awaiting-edict Heliang and others proposed changing the era name and altering the title, increasing clepsydra graduations—this could eternally settle the state.
translations.idiomatic: " Finding their words unverified, in the eighth month the emperor issued an edict: "Awaiting-edict Xia Heliang and others proposed changing the era name and title and increasing clepsydra graduations, saying this could eternally settle the state.

sentences.zh: 朕信道不篤，過聽其言，冀為百姓獲福，卒無嘉應。

translations.literal: I believed the Way without depth, excessively heard their words, hoping the hundred surnames would obtain fortune—in the end no fine response.
translations.idiomatic: I believed the Way without depth and listened too readily to their words, hoping the people would gain fortune, yet in the end there was no good response.

sentences.zh: 夫過而不改，是謂過矣！

translations.literal: To have fault yet not correct it—this is called fault indeed!
translations.idiomatic: To err and not correct the error—this is error indeed!

sentences.zh: 六月甲子詔書，非赦令，皆蠲除之。

translations.literal: The sixth-month jiazi edict documents, except amnesty orders, are all annulled.
translations.idiomatic: All edicts of the sixth-month jiazi day, except amnesty orders, are annulled.

sentences.zh: 賀良等反道惑眾，奸態當窮竟。

translations.literal: Heliang and others opposed the Way and deluded the multitude; their wicked condition ought be fully pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Heliang and others opposed the Way and deluded the multitude; their wicked conduct must be pursued to the end.

sentences.zh: 」皆下獄，伏誅。

translations.literal: " All were sent to prison and executed.
translations.idiomatic: " All were imprisoned and executed.

sentences.zh: 尋及解光減死一等，徙敦煌郡。

translations.literal: Xun and Jie Guang had their sentences reduced one grade and were exiled to Dunhuang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun and Jie Guang had their sentences reduced one grade and were exiled to Dunhuang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 上以寢疾，盡復前世所嘗興諸神祠凡七百餘所，一歲三萬七千祠雲。

translations.literal: The emperor, due to illness, fully restored all spirit shrines former ages had raised—more than seven hundred in all; thirty-seven thousand sacrifices in one year, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his illness, the emperor fully restored all the spirit shrines former ages had raised—more than seven hundred in all—and it is said there were thirty-seven thousand sacrifices in a single year.

sentences.zh: 傅太后怨傅喜不已，使孔鄉侯晏風丞相朱博令奏免喜侯。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Fu resented Fu Xi without end and had Marquis of Kongxiang Yan prompt Chancellor Zhu Bo to memorialize removing Xi's marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Fu's resentment of Fu Xi did not cease; she had Marquis of Kongxiang Fu Yan prompt Chancellor Zhu Bo to memorialize stripping Fu Xi of his marquisate.

sentences.zh: 博與御史大夫趙玄議之，玄言：「事已前決，得無不宜？

translations.literal: Bo deliberated with Censor-in-Chief Zhao Xuan; Xuan said: "The matter was already decided before—perhaps it ought not be done?
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bo deliberated with Censor-in-Chief Zhao Xuan; Xuan said: "The matter was already decided—perhaps it ought not be done?

sentences.zh: 」博曰：「已許孔鄉侯矣。

translations.literal: " Bo said: "I already promised Marquis of Kongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Bo said: "I already promised Marquis of Kongxiang.

sentences.zh: 匹夫相要，尚相得死，何況至尊！

translations.literal: Common men making mutual pledges still obtain death for one another—how much more the August Ultimate!
translations.idiomatic: When common men make mutual pledges, they still die for one another—how much more the August Ultimate!

sentences.zh: 博唯有死耳！

translations.literal: Bo has only death!
translations.idiomatic: For Zhu Bo there is only death!

sentences.zh: 」玄即許可。

translations.literal: " Xuan immediately granted assent.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao Xuan yielded.

sentences.zh: 博惡獨斥奏喜，以故大司空汜鄉侯何武前亦坐過免就國，事與喜相似，即並奏：「喜、武前在位，皆無益於治，雖已退免，爵土之封，非所當也。

translations.literal: Bo hated to impeach Xi alone; because the former Grand Minister of Works Marquis of Sìxiang He Wu had earlier also sat for an offense, been dismissed, and gone to his fief—the affair being similar to Xi's—he therefore memorialized together: "Xi and Wu, while previously in office, were both of no benefit to governance; although already dismissed and removed, enfeoffment of noble rank and fief is not what they ought to have."
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to single out Fu Xi alone, Zhu Bo lumped in He Wu, former Grand Minister of Works and Marquis of Sìxiang, who had also been cashiered to his fief: "Neither Fu Xi nor He Wu helped the government while in power; though removed, they should not keep their marquisates and lands."

sentences.zh: 皆請免為庶人。

translations.literal: We request that both be dismissed as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Strip both to commoner rank.

sentences.zh: 」上知傅太后素嘗怨喜，疑博、玄承指，即召玄詣尚書問狀，玄辭服。

translations.literal: " The emperor knew Grand Dowager Empress Fu had always resented Xi; he suspected Bo and Xuan carried out her hint; he immediately summoned Xuan to the Secretariat to question the circumstances; Xuan confessed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor knew the grand empress dowager's grudge against Fu Xi and suspected Zhu Bo and Zhao Xuan acted on her nod; he summoned Zhao Xuan to the Secretariat for questioning, and Zhao Xuan confessed.

sentences.zh: 有詔：「左將軍彭宣與中朝者雜問」，宣等奏劾「博、玄、晏皆不道，不敬，請召詣廷尉詔獄」。

translations.literal: There was an edict: "Left General Peng Xuan and inner-court officials shall jointly interrogate"; Xuan and others impeached: "Bo, Xuan, and Yan are all unfilial and irreverent—we request they be summoned to the Minister of Justice's imperial prison."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: "Left General Peng Xuan and inner-court officials shall conduct a joint hearing." Peng Xuan and colleagues impeached: "Zhu Bo, Zhao Xuan, and Ding Yan are all unfilial and irreverent—summon them to the imperial prison under the Minister of Justice."

sentences.zh: 上減玄死罪三等；

translations.literal: The emperor reduced Xuan's death penalty by three degrees;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reduced Zhao Xuan's death sentence by three degrees;

sentences.zh: 削晏戶四分之一；

translations.literal: cut Yan's household by one quarter;
translations.idiomatic: cut Ding Yan's fief household by one quarter;

sentences.zh: 假謁者節召丞相詣廷尉，博自殺，國除。

translations.literal: a provisional emissary's staff was lent to summon the chancellor to the Minister of Justice; Bo killed himself, and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: an envoy bearing the imperial staff summoned the chancellor to the Minister of Justice; Zhu Bo killed himself, and his marquisate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 九月，以光祿勳平當為御史大夫；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Director of the Secretariat Ping Dang was made Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Director of the Secretariat Ping Dang was appointed Censor-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲寅，遷為丞相；

translations.literal: in winter, the tenth month, on jiayin, he was transferred to be chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: in winter, the tenth month, on jiayin, he was promoted to chancellor;

sentences.zh: 以冬月故，且賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: because it was the winter month, he was also granted the rank of Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: because it was winter, he was also granted the rank of Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 以京兆尹平陵王喜為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Governor of the Capital Wang Xi of Pingling was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of the Capital Wang Xi of Pingling was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 上欲令丁、傅處爪牙官，是歲，策免左將軍淮陽彭宣，以關內侯歸家，而以光祿勳丁望代為左將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to place the Ding and Fu clans in claw-and-fang offices; that year he removed Left General Peng Xuan of Huaiyang by patent, sent him home as Marquis Within the Passes, and made Director of the Secretariat Ding Wang Left General in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to place the Ding and Fu clans in posts of real power; that year he removed Left General Peng Xuan of Huaiyang by patent, sent him home as Marquis Within the Passes, and made Director of the Secretariat Ding Wang Left General in his place.

sentences.zh: 烏孫卑爰疐侵盜匈奴西界，單于遣兵擊之，殺數百人，略千餘人，驅牛畜去。

translations.literal: The Wusun chieftain Beiai Zhi raided and plundered the Xiongnu western border; the chanyu sent troops to strike him, killed several hundred, captured more than a thousand, and drove off cattle and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: The Wusun chieftain Beiai Zhi raided the Xiongnu western border; the chanyu sent troops against him, killed several hundred, captured more than a thousand people, and drove off cattle and livestock.

sentences.zh: 卑爰疐恐，遣子趨逯為質匈奴，單于受，以狀聞。

translations.literal: Beiai Zhi was afraid; he sent his son Qu Lu as hostage to the Xiongnu; the chanyu accepted him and reported the matter upstream.
translations.idiomatic: Beiai Zhi was afraid; he sent his son Qu Lu as hostage to the Xiongnu; the chanyu accepted him and reported the matter to the Han court.

sentences.zh: 漢遣使者責讓單于，告令還歸卑爰疐質子。

translations.literal: Han sent an envoy to reproach the chanyu and instruct him to return Beiai Zhi's hostage son.
translations.idiomatic: The Han court sent an envoy to reproach the chanyu and ordered him to return Beiai Zhi's hostage son.

sentences.zh: 單于受詔遣歸。

translations.literal: The chanyu received the edict and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu obeyed the edict and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，立廣德夷王弟廣漢為廣平王。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the younger brother of the Yi King of Guangde, Guanghan, was established as King of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Guanghan, younger brother of the Yi King of Guangde, was established as King of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，帝太太后所居桂宮正殿火。

translations.literal: On guimao, fire broke out in the main hall of the Cassia Palace where the Emperor's Grand Dowager Empress dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, fire broke out in the main hall of the Cassia Palace where the Emperor's Grand Dowager Empress dwelt.

sentences.zh: 上使使者召丞相平當，欲封之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to summon Chancellor Ping Dang, intending to enfeoff him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to summon Chancellor Ping Dang, intending to enfeoff him.

sentences.zh: 當病篤，不應召。

translations.literal: Dang was gravely ill and did not answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Dang was gravely ill and did not answer the summons.

sentences.zh: 室家或謂當：「不可強起受侯印為子孫邪？

translations.literal: Members of his household said to Dang: "Can you not force yourself to rise and accept the marquis's seal for your descendants' sake?
translations.idiomatic: Members of his household said to Dang, "Can you not force yourself up to accept the marquis's seal for your descendants' sake?

sentences.zh: 」當日：「吾居大位，已負素餐責矣。

translations.literal: " Dang said: "I have held the great post and already bear the blame of eating salary without work.
translations.idiomatic: " Dang said, "I have held the great post and already bear the blame of eating salary without work.

sentences.zh: 起受侯印，還臥而死，死有餘罪。

translations.literal: To rise and accept the marquis's seal, then return to lie down and die—death would still leave guilt remaining.
translations.idiomatic: To rise and accept the marquis's seal, then return to bed and die—death would still leave guilt remaining.

sentences.zh: 今不起者，所以為子孫也！

translations.literal: Not rising now is precisely for my descendants' sake!
translations.idiomatic: Not rising now is precisely for my descendants' sake!

sentences.zh: 」遂上書乞骸骨，上不許。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he submitted a memorial begging to surrender his bones; the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he submitted a memorial begging to retire; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 三月，己酉，當薨。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiyou, Dang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiyou, Dang died.

sentences.zh: 有星孛於河鼓。

translations.literal: A broom star appeared at the River Drum.
translations.idiomatic: A comet appeared at the River Drum asterism.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁酉，王嘉為丞相，河南太守王崇為御史大夫。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingyou, Wang Jia was made chancellor and Grand Administrator of Henan Wang Chong Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingyou, Wang Jia was appointed chancellor and Grand Administrator of Henan Wang Chong Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 崇，京兆尹駿之子也。

translations.literal: Chong was the son of Governor of the Capital Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was the son of Governor of the Capital Jun.

sentences.zh: 嘉以時政苛急，郡國守相數有變動，乃上疏曰：「臣聞聖王之功在於得人。

translations.literal: Because government was harsh and urgent and commandery and kingdom governors and administrators frequently changed, Jia submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that the merit of a sage king lies in obtaining the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Because government was harsh and urgent and commandery and kingdom governors and administrators changed frequently, Jia submitted a memorial, saying, "Your servant has heard that a sage king's true achievement is winning the right men to serve him.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『材難，不其然與！

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Talent is hard to find—is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'Good men are hard to find—is that not the truth!

sentences.zh: 』故繼世立諸侯，像賢也。

translations.literal: ' Therefore in inheriting the generation and establishing feudal lords, one models the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: ' So when a new king enfeoffs the heir among the lords, he is choosing a pattern of virtue.

sentences.zh: 雖不能盡賢，天子為擇臣、立命卿以輔之。

translations.literal: Although they cannot all be worthy, the Son of Heaven for them selects ministers and orders established ministers to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the heir is not wholly worthy, the Son of Heaven still picks his ministers for him and appoints senior officers to guide him.

sentences.zh: 居是國也，累世尊重，然後士民之眾附焉。

translations.literal: Dwelling in such a state, generation after generation they are honored and heavy; afterward the multitude of gentlemen and commoners attaches to them.
translations.idiomatic: Respected across generations in that domain, they win the allegiance of gentry and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 是以教化行而治功立。

translations.literal: Therefore transformation by instruction proceeds and governing merit is established.
translations.idiomatic: Only then does moral instruction take hold and good government follow.

sentences.zh: 今之郡守重於古諸侯，往者致選賢材，賢材難得，拔擢可用者，或起於囚徒。

translations.literal: Today's commandery governors are weightier than ancient feudal lords; in former times they reached to select worthy talent; worthy talent was hard to obtain; those raised and promoted as usable sometimes rose from prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: A grand administrator today wields more power than a feudal lord of old; past dynasties strained to find able men, and when talent ran short they did not hesitate to promote a man straight from chains.

sentences.zh: 昔魏尚坐事系，文帝感馮唐之言，遺使持節赦其罪，拜為雲中太守，匈奴忌之。

translations.literal: In olden times Wei Shang sat in affair and was bound; Emperor Wen was moved by Feng Tang's words, sent an envoy bearing staff to pardon his crime, appointed him Grand Administrator of Yunzhong, and the Xiongnu feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shang was once jailed for an offense; Emperor Wen, persuaded by Feng Tang, sent an envoy with the imperial staff to free him and made him grand administrator of Yunzhong, to the Xiongnu's alarm.

sentences.zh: 武帝擢韓安國於徒中，拜為梁內史，骨肉以安。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu raised Han Anguo from among convicts, appointed him Inner Scribe of Liang, and flesh and bone thereby were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu pulled Han Anguo out of penal labor and named him inner scribe of Liang, and the imperial house knew peace again.

sentences.zh: 張敞為京兆尹，有罪當免，黠吏知而犯敞，敞收殺之，其家自冤，使者覆獄，劾敞賊殺人，上逮捕不下，會免；

translations.literal: Zhang Chang was Governor of the Capital; he had guilt and ought to have been dismissed; a cunning clerk knew and offended Chang; Chang seized and killed him; his household themselves called it wrong; an envoy reviewed the prison case and impeached Chang for bandit murder; the sovereign ordered arrest but did not carry it down; it happened he was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang, as governor of the capital, faced removal for an offense; a wily subordinate deliberately provoked him, and Chang had the man executed. The family cried foul; an imperial investigator reheard the case and charged Chang with malicious killing. The emperor withheld the warrant for his arrest until Chang was out of office;

sentences.zh: 亡命十數日，宣帝征敞拜為冀州刺史，卒獲其用。

translations.literal: he fled his mandate more than ten days; Emperor Xuan summoned Chang and appointed him Regional Inspector of Ji; in the end his use was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Chang then fled and hid for some weeks until Emperor Xuan recalled him as regional inspector of Ji—where he proved indispensable.

sentences.zh: 前世非私此三人，貪其材器有益於公家也。

translations.literal: Former generations did not privately favor these three men; they coveted their talents and implements as beneficial to the public house.
translations.idiomatic: Those earlier courts did not show those three men personal favor; they valued their abilities because they served the state.

sentences.zh: 孝文時，吏居官者或長子孫，以官為氏，倉氏、庫氏則倉庫吏之後也；

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaowen, among clerks dwelling in office some grew old and had sons and grandsons; they took office as surname; the Cang clan and Ku clan were afterward of granary and treasury clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen some families held the same minor post for generations until the office became their surname—the Cangs and the Kus, for instance, descend from granary and treasury clerks;

sentences.zh: 其二千石長吏亦安官樂職，然後上下相望，莫有苟且之意。

translations.literal: their two-thousand-picul senior officials also were secure in office and pleased with their posts; afterward superiors and inferiors looked to one another; none had a mind of careless expediency.
translations.idiomatic: then the two-thousand-picul men could settle into their posts with confidence; ruler and officials looked to each other in good faith, and no one nursed a merely cynical careerism.

sentences.zh: 其後稍稍變易，公卿以下傳相促急，又數改更政事，司隸、部刺史舉劾苛細，發揚陰私，吏或居官數月而退，送故迎新，交錯道路。

translations.literal: Afterward gradually there were changes; from dukes and ministers downward they passed on mutual urgency; also repeatedly they altered government affairs; the Metropolitan Superintendent and Regional Inspectors impeached with harsh minuteness, exposing and raising hidden private matters; clerks sometimes dwelt in office several months then withdrew; escorting the old and welcoming the new crisscrossed the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Little by little the climate changed: from the highest ministers down, everyone hectored everyone else; policy swung back and forth; metropolitan and regional inspectors hunted for slip-ups and dragged private faults into the open; magistrates lasted only months before transfer; processions seeing off the outgoing and greeting the incoming choked the highways.

sentences.zh: 中材苟容求全，下材懷危內顧，壹切營私者多。

translations.literal: Those of middling talent carelessly accommodated to seek completeness; those of lower talent harbored peril and looked inward; in all cases those who schemed for private gain were many.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre men played it safe to survive; lesser men watched their backs; across the board, self-dealing multiplied.

sentences.zh: 二千石益輕賤，吏民慢易之，或持其微過，增加成罪，言於刺史、司隸，或上書告之。

translations.literal: The two-thousand-picul grew ever more lightly despised; clerks and commoners treated them with contempt; some seized their slight faults, augmented them into completed guilt, and spoke to regional inspectors and the Metropolitan Superintendent, or submitted memorials to denounce them.
translations.idiomatic: The two-thousand-picul posts grew ever more lightly held; clerks and commoners treated their holders with contempt; some seized slight faults, inflated them into full charges, and denounced them to regional inspectors, the metropolitan superintendent, or the throne by memorial.

sentences.zh: 眾庶知其易危，小失意則有離畔之心。

translations.literal: The multitude knew they were easy to endanger; with a small disappointment they had a mind to separate and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The people knew their magistrates were easy to topple; at the slightest grievance they were ready to turn away.

sentences.zh: 前山陽亡徒蘇令等縱橫，吏士臨難，莫肯伏節死義，以守、相威權素奪也。

translations.literal: Earlier at Shanyang the escaped convict Su Ling and others ranged freely; when clerks and gentlemen faced peril none would submit to integrity and die for righteousness—because the governors' and administrators' authority and power had long since been stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier at Shanyang the escaped convict Su Ling and others ran riot; when officials faced danger none would stand firm and die for duty—because the governors' and administrators' authority had long since been stripped away.

sentences.zh: 孝成皇帝悔之，下詔書，二千石不為故縱，遣使者賜金，尉厚其意，誠以為國家有急，取辦於二千石；

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaocheng regretted it and issued an edict: two-thousand-picul officials were not to connive in old indulgence; he sent envoys to bestow gold and comfort and thicken their intent, truly thinking that when the state had urgency he would obtain results from the two-thousand-picul;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng regretted it and issued an edict: two-thousand-picul officials were not to connive in old indulgence; he sent envoys to bestow gold and reassure them, truly thinking that when the state had urgency he would obtain results from the two-thousand-picul;

sentences.zh: 二千石尊重難危，乃能使下。

translations.literal: when the two-thousand-picul were honored, weighty, hard to endanger, only then could they make inferiors obey.
translations.idiomatic: only when the two-thousand-picul were honored, weighty, and hard to endanger could they make inferiors obey.

sentences.zh: 孝宣皇帝愛其善治民之吏，有章劾事留中，會赦壹解。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoxuan loved his officials who governed the people well; when there were memorial impeachments the matter was held within; when an amnesty came it was once released.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan loved officials who governed the people well; when impeachment memorials arrived he held them within; when an amnesty came he released the matter once.

sentences.zh: 故事：尚書希下章，為煩擾百姓，證驗系治，或死獄中，章文必有『敢告之』字乃下。

translations.literal: By precedent: the Secretariat rarely forwarded memorials downward, lest the people be troubled and disturbed; verification and binding for trial sometimes ended in death in prison; only when the memorial text had the words 'dare to report this' would it be sent down.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the Secretariat rarely forwarded denunciation memorials, lest the people be harassed; verification and trial sometimes ended in death in prison; only when the memorial text contained the words 'dare to report this' would it be sent down.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下留神於擇賢，記善忘過，容忍臣子，勿責以備。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty keep your mind on selecting the worthy, record good deeds and forget faults, tolerate your ministers and sons, and not demand completeness.
translations.idiomatic: Only may Your Majesty keep your mind on selecting the worthy, record good deeds and forget faults, tolerate your ministers, and not demand perfection.

sentences.zh: 二千石、部刺史、三輔縣令有材任職者，人情不能不有過差，宜可闊略，令盡力者有所勸。

translations.literal: Among two-thousand-picul officials, Regional Inspectors, and the three metropolitan auxiliaries' county magistrates who have talent and fit their posts, human feeling cannot fail to have faults and slips—it is fitting to be broad and spare, so that those who exhaust their strength may have encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Among two-thousand-picul officials, regional inspectors, and metropolitan county magistrates who have talent and fit their posts, human nature cannot fail to slip—it is fitting to be broad and spare, so that those who give their utmost may be encouraged.

sentences.zh: 此方今急務，國家之利也。

translations.literal: This is the urgent task of the present moment and the profit of the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is the urgent task of the moment and the state's profit.

sentences.zh: 前蘇令發，欲遣大夫使逐問狀，時見大夫無可使者，召盩厔令尹逢，拜為諫大夫遣之。

translations.literal: Earlier when Su Ling rose up, the court wished to send a grandee as envoy to pursue and question the circumstances; at the time no grandee was seen who could be sent; Zhìzhì Magistrate Yin Feng was summoned, appointed Remonstrance Grandee, and dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier when Su Ling rose up, the court wished to send a grandee to pursue and investigate; at the time no suitable grandee could be found; Zhìzhì Magistrate Yin Feng was summoned, appointed Remonstrance Grandee, and dispatched.

sentences.zh: 今諸大夫有材能者甚少，宜豫畜養可成就者，則士赴難不愛其死。

translations.literal: Now among the various grandees those with talent and ability are very few; it is fitting beforehand to rear and nurture those who can be brought to completion—then gentlemen facing peril will not be sparing of their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Now able grandees are very few; it is fitting beforehand to rear and nurture those who can be brought to completion—then gentlemen facing peril will not spare their lives.

sentences.zh: 臨事倉卒乃求，非所以明朝廷也。

translations.literal: To seek only when affairs come in haste is not the means by which to clarify the court.
translations.idiomatic: To seek men only when crisis comes in haste is not how to clarify the court.

sentences.zh: 」嘉因薦儒者公孫光、滿昌及能吏蕭鹹、薛修等，皆故二千石有名稱者，天子納而用之。

translations.literal: " Jia thereupon recommended the Confucians Gongsun Guang and Man Chang and able administrators Xiao Xian and Xue Xiu and others—all former two-thousand-picul men of famous reputation; the Son of Heaven accepted and employed them.
translations.idiomatic: " Jia thereupon recommended the Confucians Gongsun Guang and Man Chang and able administrators Xiao Xian and Xue Xiu and others—all former two-thousand-picul men of famous reputation; the emperor accepted and employed them.

sentences.zh: 六月，立魯頃王子部鄉侯閔為王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Bu Village Marquis Min, son of King Qing of Lu, was established as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Bu Village Marquis Min, son of King Qing of Lu, was established as king.

sentences.zh: 上以寢疾未定，冬，十一月，壬子，令太皇太后下詔復甘泉泰畤、汾陰后土祠，罷南、北郊。

translations.literal: Because the emperor's lingering illness was not settled, in winter, the eleventh month, on renzi, he had the Grand Empress Dowager issue an edict restoring sacrifice at Sweet Springs' Great Altars and Fenyin's Queen of Earth shrine, and abolishing the southern and northern suburban sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor's lingering illness was not settled, in winter, the eleventh month, on renzi, he had the Grand Empress Dowager issue an edict restoring sacrifice at Sweet Springs' Great Altars and Fenyin's Queen of Earth shrine, and abolishing the southern and northern suburban sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 上亦不能親至甘泉、河東，遣有司行事而禮祠焉。

translations.literal: The emperor also could not personally go to Sweet Springs and Hedong; he sent the responsible offices to perform the rites and sacrifice there.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also could not personally go to Sweet Springs and Hedong; he sent the responsible offices to perform the rites and sacrifice there.

sentences.zh: 無鹽危山土自起覆草，如馳道狀；

translations.literal: At Mount Wei in Wuyan, earth of itself rose and covered grass in the shape of an imperial processional road;
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Wei in Wuyan, earth of itself rose and covered grass in the shape of an imperial processional road;

sentences.zh: 又，瓠山石轉立。

translations.literal: also, at Mount Hu a stone turned and stood upright.
translations.idiomatic: also, at Mount Hu a stone turned and stood upright.

sentences.zh: 東平王雲及後謁自之石所祭，治石像瓠山立石，束倍草，並祠之。

translations.literal: King Yun of Dongping and Queen Ye personally went to the stone place to sacrifice; they fashioned a stone like the standing stone at Mount Hu, bound double handfuls of grass, and sacrificed to both.
translations.idiomatic: King Yun of Dongping and Queen Ye personally went to the stone to sacrifice; they fashioned a stone like the standing stone at Mount Hu, bound double handfuls of grass, and sacrificed to both.

sentences.zh: 河內息夫躬、長安孫寵相與謀共告之，曰：「此取封侯之計也。

translations.literal: Xi Fu Gong of Henei and Sun Chong of Chang'an plotted together to denounce them, saying: "This is the stratagem for obtaining enfeoffment as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Fu Gong of Henei and Sun Chong of Chang'an plotted together to denounce them, saying, "This is the stratagem for obtaining enfeoffment as marquis.

sentences.zh: 」乃與中郎谷師譚共因中常侍宋弘上變事，告焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon together with Palace Gentleman Gu Shi Tan, through Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary Song Hong, they submitted a report of anomaly and denounced them.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon together with Palace Gentleman Gu Shi Tan, through Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary Song Hong, they submitted a report of anomaly and denounced them.

sentences.zh: 是時上被疾，多所惡，事下有司，逮王后謁下獄驗治；

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was afflicted with illness and hated many things; the matter was sent down to the responsible offices; Queen Ye was arrested and put in prison for verification and trial;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was ill and prone to suspicion; the matter was sent down to the responsible offices; Queen Ye was arrested and imprisoned for investigation;

sentences.zh: 服「祠祭詛祝上，為雲求為天子，以為石立，宣帝起之表也。

translations.literal: she confessed: "In sacrifice and prayer I cursed and wished harm on the sovereign, sought the kingship for Yun, and took the stone's standing as the omen by which Emperor Xuan rose."
translations.idiomatic: she confessed: "In sacrifice and prayer I cursed the sovereign, sought the kingship for Yun, and took the stone's standing as the omen by which Emperor Xuan rose."

sentences.zh: 」有司請誅王，有詔，廢徙房陵。

translations.literal: " The responsible offices requested execution of the king; there was an edict to depose him and move him to Fangling.
translations.idiomatic: " The responsible offices requested execution of the king; an edict deposed him and moved him to Fangling.

sentences.zh: 雲自殺，謁並舅伍宏及成帝舅安成共侯夫人放，皆棄市。

translations.literal: Yun killed himself; Ye, her maternal uncle Wu Hong, and the wife of Marquis of Gong of Ancheng Fang—Emperor Cheng's maternal uncle—were all executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Yun killed himself; Ye, her maternal uncle Wu Hong, and the wife of Marquis of Gong of Ancheng Fang—Emperor Cheng's maternal uncle—were all executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 事連御史大夫王崇，左遷大司農。

translations.literal: The affair implicated Censor-in-Chief Wang Chong, who was demoted to Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: The affair implicated Censor-in-Chief Wang Chong, who was demoted to Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 擢寵為南陽太守，譚穎川都尉，弘、躬皆光祿大夫、左曹、給事中。

translations.literal: Chong was promoted to Grand Administrator of Nanyang; Tan made Commandant of Yingchuan; Hong and Gong were all made Palace Chamberlains, Left Bureau, and Attendants Within.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was promoted to Grand Administrator of Nanyang; Tan made Commandant of Yingchuan; Hong and Gong were all made Palace Chamberlains, Left Bureau, and Attendants Within.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，大旱。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, there was great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, there was great drought.

sentences.zh: 關東民無故驚走，持藳或掫一枚，轉相付與，曰行西王母籌，道中相過逢，多至千數，或被發徒跣，或夜折關，或逾牆入，或乘車騎奔馳，以置驛傳行，經歷郡國二十六至京師，不可禁止。

translations.literal: East of the Pass the people for no reason were startled and ran; they held straw or one stalk of grain and passed them on to one another, saying they were carrying the Queen Mother of the West's tallies; meeting one another on the road, sometimes as many as a thousand; some with hair unbound and barefoot, some breaking through gates at night, some climbing walls to enter, some riding carriages and horses in furious gallop—placing them at relay stations for transmission—passing through twenty-six commanderies and kingdoms to reach the capital; it could not be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Pass the people for no reason panicked and ran; they held straw or a single stalk and passed them along, saying they carried the Queen Mother of the West's tallies; they met on the roads in groups sometimes of a thousand; some ran with hair unbound and barefoot, some broke through gates at night, some climbed walls, some rode in furious gallop—posting the tokens at relay stations—passing through twenty-six commanderies and kingdoms to the capital; nothing could stop them.

sentences.zh: 民又聚會里巷阡陌，設張博具，歌舞祠西王母，至秋乃止。

translations.literal: The people also gathered in lanes and crossroads of villages, set out mats and gambling implements, and sang and danced to sacrifice to the Queen Mother of the West—it only stopped in autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The people also gathered in village lanes and crossroads, set out mats and gambling implements, and sang and danced to worship the Queen Mother of the West—it only stopped in autumn.

sentences.zh: 上欲封傅太后從父弟侍中、光祿大夫商，尚書僕射平陵鄭崇諫曰：「孝成皇帝封親舅五侯，天為赤黃，晝昏，日中有黑氣。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to enfeoff Grand Dowager Empress Fu's younger cousin by the same mother, Attendant Within and Palace Chamberlain Shang; Vice Director of the Secretariat Zheng Chong of Pingling remonstrated, saying: "When Emperor Xiaocheng enfeoffed his maternal uncles as the Five Marquises, Heaven turned red and yellow, day grew dim, and there was black qi within the sun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to enfeoff Grand Dowager Empress Fu's younger cousin by the same mother, Attendant Within and Palace Chamberlain Shang; Vice Director of the Secretariat Zheng Chong of Pingling remonstrated, saying, "When Emperor Cheng enfeoffed his maternal uncles as the Five Marquises, Heaven turned red and yellow, day grew dim, and there was black vapor within the sun.

sentences.zh: 孔鄉侯，皇后父，高武侯以三公封，尚有因緣。

translations.literal: Marquis of Kongxiang was the empress's father; Marquis of Gaowu was enfeoffed as one of the Three Dukes—there was still some cause and connection.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Kongxiang was the empress's father; Marquis of Gaowu was enfeoffed as one of the Three Dukes—there was still some justification.

sentences.zh: 今無故欲復封商，壞亂制度，逆天人之心，非傅氏之福也！

translations.literal: Now without cause you wish again to enfeoff Shang—this ruins and disorders the system, goes against Heaven and men's hearts, and is not the Fu clan's blessing!
translations.idiomatic: Now without cause you wish again to enfeoff Shang—this ruins the system, goes against Heaven and men's hearts, and is not the Fu clan's blessing!

sentences.zh: 臣願以身命當國咎！

translations.literal: Your servant is willing to stake body and life against the state's blame!
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is willing to stake his life against the state's blame!

sentences.zh: 」崇因持詔書案起。

translations.literal: " Chong thereupon seized the edict document from the desk and rose.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong thereupon seized the edict document from the desk and rose.

sentences.zh: 傅太后大怒曰：「何有為天子乃反為一臣所顓制邪！

translations.literal: Grand Dowager Empress Fu was greatly angry and said: "How can it be that one who is Son of Heaven is instead turned and controlled by a single minister!
translations.idiomatic: Grand Dowager Empress Fu was furious and said, "How can the Son of Heaven be turned and controlled by a single minister!

sentences.zh: 二月，癸卯，上遂下詔封商為汝昌侯。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guimao, the emperor thereupon issued an edict enfeoffing Shang as Marquis of Ruchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guimao, the emperor issued an edict enfeoffing Shang as Marquis of Ruchang.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉、侍中雲陽董賢得幸於上，出則參乘，入御左右，賞賜累巨萬，貴震朝廷。

translations.literal: Commandant of Cavalry for the Emperor's Son-in-Law and Attendant Within Dong Xian of Yunyang won the emperor's favor; going out he shared the carriage, entering he attended at the ruler's side; rewards piled to tens of thousands; his nobility shook the court.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Cavalry for the Emperor's Son-in-Law and Attendant Within Dong Xian of Yunyang won the emperor's favor; going out he shared the imperial carriage, entering he attended at the ruler's side; rewards piled to tens of thousands; his eminence shook the court.

sentences.zh: 常與上臥起。

translations.literal: He often slept and rose with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He often shared the emperor's couch.

sentences.zh: 嘗晝寢，偏藉上袖，上欲起，賢未覺，不欲動賢，乃斷袖而起。

translations.literal: Once during a daytime nap he lay partly on the emperor's sleeve; the emperor wished to rise but Xian had not awakened; not wishing to disturb Xian, he cut the sleeve and rose.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor napped with him; Xian lay across his sleeve. Rather than wake him, the emperor cut the cloth free and rose.

sentences.zh: 又詔賢妻得通引籍殿中，止賢廬。

translations.literal: He also edicted that Xian's wife might hold passage credentials into the palace and lodge in Xian's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He also edicted that Dong Xian's wife might carry palace passes and lodge in his quarters within the palace.

sentences.zh: 又召賢女弟以為昭儀，位次皇后。

translations.literal: He also summoned Xian's younger sister to be Lady of Handsome Deportment, ranking next to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: He also took Dong Xian's younger sister as Lady of Handsome Deportment, second only to the empress.

sentences.zh: 昭儀及賢與妻旦夕上下，並侍左右。

translations.literal: The Lady of Handsome Deportment, Xian, and his wife attended morning and evening above and below, all serving at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: The sister, Dong Xian, and his wife attended the emperor morning and night, all at his side.

sentences.zh: 以賢父恭為少府，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Xian's father Gong was made Privy Treasurer and granted the rank of Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xian's father Gong was made Privy Treasurer and granted the rank of Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 詔將作大匠為賢起大第北闕下，重殿，洞門，土木之功，窮極技巧。

translations.literal: He edicted the Master of Works to build a great mansion for Xian below the North Gate Tower—double halls, cavernous gates; earth and timber work exhausted the utmost in skill.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Master of Works to build a great mansion for Dong Xian below the North Gate Tower—double halls, cavernous gates; the carpentry exhausted every refinement of skill.

sentences.zh: 賜武庫禁兵，上方珍寶。

translations.literal: He bestowed arsenal forbidden troops and the sovereign's upper treasures.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed arsenal guards and the sovereign's choicest treasures.

sentences.zh: 其選物上弟盡在董氏，而乘輿所服乃其副也。

translations.literal: The choicest of selected goods of the highest grade were all in the Dong clan, while what the imperial carriage wore was only the secondary.
translations.idiomatic: The choicest of selected goods were all in the Dong clan, while what the emperor wore was only the secondary lot.

sentences.zh: 及至東園秘器、珠襦、玉柙，豫以賜賢，無不備具。

translations.literal: Even reaching the Eastern Garden secret fittings, pearl shroud, and jade casings—they were beforehand bestowed on Xian, nothing lacking or incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Eastern Garden funeral fittings, pearl shroud, and jade casings were bestowed on Dong Xian in advance, nothing lacking.

sentences.zh: 又令將作為賢起塚塋義陵旁，內為便房，剛柏題湊，外為徼道，周垣數里，門闕罘罳甚盛。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Master of Works to raise a tomb mound for Xian beside Yiling; within were convenient chambers with cypress beams joined at the heads; without were patrol paths; the encircling wall ran several li; gate towers and patterned screens were very grand.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the Master of Works to raise a tomb for Dong Xian beside Yiling; within were side chambers with cypress beams joined at the heads; without were patrol paths; the encircling wall ran several li; gate towers and patterned screens were very grand.

sentences.zh: 鄭崇以賢貴寵過度諫上，由是重得罪，數以職事見責；

translations.literal: Zheng Chong, because Xian's nobility and favor were excessive, remonstrated with the emperor; because of this he again incurred heavy guilt and was repeatedly blamed on official business;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chong remonstrated that Dong Xian's favor was excessive; because of this he again incurred heavy guilt and was repeatedly blamed on official business;

sentences.zh: 發疾頸癰，欲乞骸骨，不敢。

translations.literal: an illness broke out—a carbuncle on the neck; he wished to beg to surrender his bones but did not dare.
translations.idiomatic: a carbuncle broke out on his neck; he wished to beg to retire but did not dare.

sentences.zh: 尚書令趙昌佞諂，素害崇；

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Zhao Chang was fawning and sycophantic and had always harmed Chong;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Zhao Chang was fawning and sycophantic and had always hated Chong;

sentences.zh: 知見疏，因奏「崇與宗族通，疑有奸，請治。

translations.literal: knowing Chong was estranged, he therefore memorialized: "Chong has relations with his clan kin—suspected of impropriety—we request investigation.
translations.idiomatic: knowing Chong was estranged, he memorialized: "Chong has relations with his clan kin—suspected of impropriety—we request investigation.

sentences.zh: 」上責崇曰：「君門如市人，何以欲禁切主上？

translations.literal: " The emperor reproached Chong, saying: "Your gate is like a market of people—why do you wish to restrict and control the lord above?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor reproached Zheng Chong, saying, "Your gate is like a thronged market—why do you wish to restrict and control your sovereign?

sentences.zh: 」崇對曰：「臣門如市，臣心如水。

translations.literal: " Chong replied, saying: "Your subject's gate is like a market; your subject's heart is like water.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong replied, "Your subject's gate may be like a market, but your subject's heart is like water.

sentences.zh: 願得考覆！

translations.literal: May I receive investigation and verification!
translations.idiomatic: I ask to be investigated and verified!

sentences.zh: 」上怒，下崇獄。

translations.literal: " The emperor was angry and sent Chong down to prison.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was furious and sent Chong to prison.

sentences.zh: 司隸孫寶上書曰：「按尚書令昌奏僕射崇獄，覆治，榜掠將死，卒無一辭，道路稱冤。

translations.literal: Director of the Retainers Sun Bao submitted a memorial, saying: "According to the memorial of Master of Documents Chang on Vice Director Chong's prison case, re-investigation was made; beating and flogging nearly killed him, yet in the end not one word was spoken—on the roads they call it wrongful.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Retainers Sun Bao memorialized, saying, "Per Master of Documents Zhao Chang's memorial on Vice Director Chong's case, re-investigation was conducted; beating and flogging nearly killed him, yet he would not speak a word—the people on the roads call it wrongful.

sentences.zh: 疑昌與崇內有纖介，浸潤相陷。

translations.literal: It is suspected that Chang and Chong had a fine grudge within, soaking and seeping to trap each other.
translations.idiomatic: I suspect Chang and Chong harbored a petty grudge and slandered each other into ruin.

sentences.zh: 自禁門樞機近臣，蒙受冤譖，虧損國家，為謗不小。

translations.literal: From the forbidden gates and pivot of power, close ministers receiving wrongful slander damages the state—the slander is not small.
translations.idiomatic: When close ministers at the pivot of power suffer wrongful slander, the state is harmed—and the scandal is no small matter.

sentences.zh: 臣請治昌以解眾心。

translations.literal: Your subject requests that Chang be punished to settle the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject requests that Chang be punished to settle public anger.

sentences.zh: 免寶為庶人。

translations.literal: Bao was dismissed and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was dismissed and reduced to commoner status.
