translations.idiomatic: " Chong died in prison.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁卯，諸吏、散騎、光祿勳賈延為御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the second month, on dingmao, Gentleman-Attendant, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Household Minister of the Imperial Clan Jia Yan was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingmao, Jia Yan—formerly Gentleman-Attendant, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Household Minister of the Imperial Clan—was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 上欲侯董賢而未有緣，侍中傅嘉勸上定息夫躬、孫寵告東平本章，掇去宋弘，更言因董賢以聞，欲以其功侯之，皆先賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to enfeoff Dong Xian but had no occasion; Attendant-in-Ordinary Fu Jia urged the emperor to fix the original memorial of Xinfu Gong and Sun Chong reporting the Prince of Dongping's plot, pick out and remove Song Hong, change the account to say it came to attention through Dong Xian, wishing to enfeoff him for this merit—all were first granted rank as Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to enfeoff Dong Xian but lacked a pretext; Attendant-in-Ordinary Fu Jia urged him to settle the original memorial in which Xinfu Gong and Sun Chong reported the Prince of Dongping's plot, remove Song Hong from the credit, and recast the account so that Dong Xian brought it to attention, intending to enfeoff him for the merit—all three were first granted rank as marquises within the passes.

sentences.zh: 頃之，上欲封賢等而心憚王嘉，乃先使孔鄉侯晏持詔書示丞相、御史。

translations.literal: Shortly after, the emperor wished to enfeoff Xian and the others but inwardly feared Wang Jia; he thereupon first sent Marquis of Kongxiang Yan bearing the edict to show the Chancellor and Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, the emperor wished to enfeoff Xian and the others but feared Wang Jia; he first sent Marquis of Kongxiang Yan with the edict to show the Chancellor and Censor.

sentences.zh: 於是嘉與御史大夫賈延上封事言：「竊見董賢等三人始賜爵，眾庶匈匈，鹹曰賢貴，其餘並蒙恩，至今流言未解。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jia and Censor-in-Chief Jia Yan submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "Your subjects have seen that when Dong Xian and the other three men were first granted rank, the common people were clamorous; all said Xian was honored, the rest likewise received grace—down to the present rumor has not been resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jia and Censor-in-Chief Jia Yan submitted a sealed memorial, saying, "Your subjects observe that when Dong Xian and the other three were first granted rank, the people were in an uproar; all said Xian was being honored and the rest likewise favored—rumor has not subsided to this day.

sentences.zh: 陛下仁恩於賢等不已，宜暴賢等本奏語言，延問公卿、大夫、博士、議郎，考合古今，明正其義，然後乃加爵土；

translations.literal: Your Majesty's benevolent grace toward Xian and the others is unceasing; it is fitting to expose the original memorial language of Xian and the others, extend inquiry to the Three Dukes, Grand Masters, Erudites, and Remonstrance Officers, examine and join antiquity and the present, clarify and rectify its meaning, and only then add noble land;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's grace toward Xian and the others is unceasing; you should publish the original memorial language, extend inquiry to the Three Dukes, grand masters, erudites, and remonstrance officers, examine antiquity and the present to clarify the right of it, and only then add noble lands;

sentences.zh: 不然，恐大失眾心，海內引領而議。

translations.literal: if not, I fear greatly losing the hearts of the multitude—the within the seas will crane their necks and discuss.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise I fear you will greatly lose popular support and all within the seas will crane their necks in debate.

sentences.zh: 暴評其事，必有言當封者，在陛下所從；

translations.literal: Exposing and judging the matter, there will surely be those who say they ought to be enfeoffed—the choice lies with what Your Majesty follows;
translations.idiomatic: Once the matter is exposed and debated, some will surely say they ought to be enfeoffed—the choice will lie with what Your Majesty follows;

sentences.zh: 天下雖不說，咎有所分，不獨在陛下。

translations.literal: though all under Heaven may be displeased, blame will have its share—not borne by Your Majesty alone.
translations.idiomatic: though all under Heaven may be displeased, blame will be shared—not borne by Your Majesty alone.

sentences.zh: 前定陵侯淳于長初封，其事亦議，大司農谷永以長當封；

translations.literal: Previously when Marquis of Dingling Chunyu Chang was first enfeoffed, the matter was also debated; Grand Minister of Agriculture Gu Yong held that Chang ought to be enfeoffed;
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis of Dingling Chunyu Chang was first enfeoffed, the matter was also debated; Grand Minister of Agriculture Gu Yong held that Chang deserved enfeoffment;

sentences.zh: 眾人歸咎於永，先帝不獨蒙其譏。

translations.literal: the multitude placed blame on Yong; the former emperor did not alone bear the criticism.
translations.idiomatic: the multitude blamed Yong; the former emperor did not bear the criticism alone.

sentences.zh: 臣嘉，臣延，材駑不稱，死有餘責，知順指不迕，可得容身須臾。

translations.literal: Your subjects Jia and Yan—talent is dull and does not match our posts; death would still leave guilt remaining; we know that following cues and not opposing could gain us a moment's lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Your subjects Jia and Yan are dull and unfit for our posts and deserve death; we know that following your cues without opposition could gain us a moment's safety.

sentences.zh: 所以不敢者，思報厚恩也。

translations.literal: The reason we dare not is that we think to repay thick grace.
translations.idiomatic: We dare not because we wish to repay your great grace.

sentences.zh: 」上不得已，且為之止。

translations.literal: " The emperor had no choice and for the time being stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor had no choice and for the time being held off.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，尊帝太太后為皇太太后。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, the emperor's Grand Grand Empress Dowager was honored as Imperial Grand Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, the emperor's Grand Grand Empress Dowager was honored as Imperial Grand Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，辛卯，上下詔切責公卿曰：「昔楚有子玉得臣，晉文為之側席而坐；

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on xinmao, above and below an edict sharply reproached the Three Dukes, saying: "In antiquity Chu had Ziyu, Cheng of Chu, and Duke Wen of Jin for his sake sat sideways on his mat;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on xinmao, an edict sharply reproached the high ministers, saying, "In antiquity Chu had Ziyu, Cheng of Chu, and Duke Wen of Jin sat sideways on his mat for fear of him;

sentences.zh: 近事，汲黯折淮南之謀。

translations.literal: a recent case: Ji An broke the plot of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: in recent times Ji An thwarted the plot of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 今東平王雲等至有圖弒天子逆亂之謀者，是公卿股肱莫能悉心、務聰明以銷厭未萌故也。

translations.literal: Now the Prince of Dongping Yun and others reached the point of plotting regicide and rebellion against the Son of Heaven—this is because the Three Dukes, your arms and thighs, could not exhaust their hearts and strive to be perceptive to extinguish and suppress what had not yet sprouted.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Prince of Dongping Yun and others came to plot regicide and rebellion—this is because you, the high ministers who are the emperor's arms and thighs, could not devote yourselves and use your wisdom to extinguish evil before it sprouted.

sentences.zh: 賴宗廟之靈，侍中、駙馬都尉賢等發覺以聞，鹹伏厥辜。

translations.literal: Relying on the ancestral temples' numinous power, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commandant of Cavalry Dong Xian and others discovered and reported it—all submitted to their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: By the numinous power of the ancestral temples, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commandant of Cavalry Dong Xian and others discovered and reported it—all submitted to their guilt.

sentences.zh: 《書》不雲乎：『用德章厥善。

translations.literal: Does not the Documents say: 'Employ virtue to make manifest their goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Book of Documents say, 'Employ virtue to make manifest their goodness.

sentences.zh: 』其封賢為高安侯，南陽太守寵為方陽侯，左曹、光祿大夫躬為宜陵侯，賜右師譚爵關內侯。

translations.literal: ' Enfeoff Xian as Marquis of Gao'an, Nanyang Administrator Chong as Marquis of Fangyang, Left Censor and Household Minister of the Imperial Clan Gong as Marquis of Yiling, and grant Right Mentor Tan rank as Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: ' Enfeoff Xian as Marquis of Gao'an, Nanyang Administrator Sun Chong as Marquis of Fangyang, Left Censor and Household Minister Xinfu Gong as Marquis of Yiling, and grant Right Mentor Tan rank as marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 」又封傅太后同母弟鄭惲子業為陽信侯。

translations.idiomatic: " Moreover, Grand Empress Dowager Fu's uterine brother Zheng Yun's son Ye was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangxin.

sentences.zh: 息夫躬既親近，數進見言事，議論無所避，上疏歷詆公卿大臣。

translations.literal: Xinfu Gong being already intimate, repeatedly entered audience to speak on affairs; in discussion he avoided nothing and in memorials to the throne serially denounced the Three Dukes and great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Xinfu Gong, being intimate with the emperor, repeatedly entered audience to speak on affairs, held back nothing in debate, and in memorials serially denounced the high ministers.

sentences.zh: 眾畏其口，見之仄目。

translations.literal: The multitude feared his mouth; seeing him they narrowed their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone feared his tongue and narrowed their eyes when they saw him.

sentences.zh: 上使中黃門發武庫兵，前後十輩，送董賢及上乳母王阿捨。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Palace Attendants of the Yellow Gates to issue arms from the Arsenal, ten batches before and after, to deliver to Dong Xian and the emperor's wet nurse Wang A.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Palace Attendants to issue arms from the Arsenal in ten batches, for Dong Xian and the emperor's wet nurse Wang A.

sentences.zh: 執金吾毋將隆奏言：「武庫兵器，天下公用。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Capital Wujiang Long memorialized, saying: "Arsenal weapons are for public use under all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the Capital Wujiang Long memorialized, saying, "Arsenal weapons are for public use throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 國家武備，繕治造作，皆度大司農錢。

translations.literal: The state's military preparedness—repair, governance, and manufacture—all measure out Grand Minister of Agriculture funds.
translations.idiomatic: The state's military preparedness—repair and manufacture—all draw on Grand Minister of Agriculture funds.

sentences.zh: 大司農錢，自乘輿不以給共養；

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Agriculture funds—from the imperial carriage onward are not used to supply maintenance;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Agriculture funds are not used even for the imperial carriage's maintenance;

sentences.zh: 共養勞賜，一出少府。

translations.literal: maintenance, labor grants, and gifts all come solely from the Privy Purse.
translations.idiomatic: maintenance, labor grants, and gifts all come solely from the Privy Purse.

sentences.zh: 蓋不以本臧給末用，不以民力共浮費，別公私，示正路也。

translations.literal: In sum, not using root stores to supply terminal uses, not using the people's strength for floating expenses—separating public and private shows the correct path.
translations.idiomatic: This is so as not to supply minor expenses from root stores or burden the people with frivolous costs—separating public and private shows the correct path.

sentences.zh: 古者諸侯、方伯得顓征伐，乃賜斧鉞，漢家邊吏職任距寇，亦賜武庫兵，皆任事然後蒙之。

translations.literal: In antiquity when feudal lords and regional commissioners obtained sole authority to campaign and punish, only then were axe and yue bestowed; in Han, border officials whose duty was to repel invaders likewise received Arsenal arms—all only after assuming office did they receive them.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity feudal lords and regional commissioners who held sole authority to campaign received axe and yue; in Han, border officials charged with repelling invaders likewise received Arsenal arms—only after assuming office.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之誼，家不臧甲，所以抑臣威，損私力也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals' principle: a household does not store armor—this is to restrain ministers' authority and diminish private power.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn principle is that a household does not store armor—to restrain ministers' authority and diminish private power.

sentences.zh: 今賢等便僻弄臣，私恩微妾，而以天下公用給其私門，契國威器，共其家備，民力分於弄臣，武兵設於微妾，建立非宜，以廣驕僭，非所以示四方也。

translations.literal: Now Xian and the others are fawning, crooked court favorites and private grace to humble concubines—yet with what is publicly used under all under Heaven they supply their private gates, carving out the state's awesome implements to share their household stores; the people's strength is divided among favorites, martial arms set up for humble concubines—establishment is not fitting, to broaden arrogance and overstepping; this is not how to show the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xian and the others are fawning favorites and objects of private favor to humble concubines—yet public arms of the realm supply their private gates, carving out the state's awesome weapons for their household stores; the people's strength is divided among favorites and martial arms set up for concubines—this is improper, broadens arrogance and overstepping, and is not how to show the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『奚取於三家之堂！

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'What does he take from the Hall of the Three Families!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'What does he take from the Hall of the Three Families!

sentences.zh: 』臣請收還武庫。

translations.literal: ' Your subject requests that they be collected and returned to the Arsenal.
translations.idiomatic: ' Your subject requests that they be collected and returned to the Arsenal.

sentences.zh: 」上不說。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 頃之，傅太后使謁者賤買執金吾官婢八人，隆奏言：「買賤，請更平直。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Grand Empress Dowager Fu sent an usher to buy cheaply eight official slave women of the Commandant of the Capital; Long memorialized, saying: "The purchase was cheap—please make it more fair and straight.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, Grand Empress Dowager Fu sent an usher to buy eight official slave women of the Commandant of the Capital at a low price; Long memorialized, "The purchase was too cheap—please set a fair price.

sentences.zh: 」上於是制詔丞相、御史：「隆位九卿，既無以匡朝廷之不逮，而反奏請與永信宮爭貴賤之賈，傷化失俗。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon issued an edict to the Chancellor and Censor: "Long holds rank among the Nine Ministers, yet could not correct the court's shortcomings and instead memorialized to contend with Yongxin Palace over the price high and low—injuring transformation and losing custom.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon issued an edict to the Chancellor and Censor: "Long holds rank among the Nine Ministers, yet could not correct the court's shortcomings and instead memorialized to haggle with Yongxin Palace over price—injuring morals and offending custom.

sentences.zh: 以隆前有安國之言，左遷為沛郡都尉。

translations.literal: Because Long earlier had words that stabilized the state, he was demoted to be Commandant of Pei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because Long earlier had counseled that stabilized the state, he was demoted to Commandant of Pei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 」初，成帝末，隆為諫大夫，嘗奏封事言：「古者選諸侯入為公卿，以褒功德，宜征定陶王使在國邸，以填萬方。

translations.literal: " At the beginning, at the end of Emperor Cheng's reign, Long was Remonstrance Officer and once submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "In antiquity feudal lords were selected to enter service as the Three Dukes to praise merit and virtue; it is fitting to summon the King of Dingtao to remain at the state lodge to fill the ten thousand directions.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, at the end of Emperor Cheng's reign, Long was Remonstrance Officer and once submitted a sealed memorial, saying, "In antiquity feudal lords were selected to serve as the Three Dukes to honor merit; the King of Dingtao should be summoned to remain at the state lodge to secure the realm.

sentences.zh: 」故上思其言而宥之。

translations.literal: " Therefore the emperor recalled his words and spared him.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore the emperor recalled his counsel and spared him.

sentences.zh: 諫大夫渤海鮑宣上書曰：「竊見孝成皇帝時，外親持權，人人牽引所私以充塞朝廷，妨賢人路，濁亂天下，奢泰亡度，窮困百姓，是以日食且十，彗星四起。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Officer Bao Xuan of Bohai submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject has seen that in Emperor Cheng's time, maternal kin held power; each man drew in his private favorites to fill and block the court, obstructing the path of worthy men, muddying and disordering all under Heaven, extravagance without limit, exhausting the hundred surnames—therefore solar eclipses came to nearly ten and comets rose in four places.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Officer Bao Xuan of Bohai memorialized, saying, "Your subject observes that under Emperor Cheng, maternal kin held power; each man drew in private favorites to fill the court, blocked worthy men, muddied and disordered the realm, and spent without limit until the people were exhausted—therefore solar eclipses came to nearly ten and comets appeared in four quarters.

sentences.zh: 危亡之征，陛下所親見也；

translations.literal: Signs of peril and ruin—Your Majesty has personally seen them;
translations.idiomatic: Signs of peril and ruin—Your Majesty has seen them with your own eyes;

sentences.zh: 今奈何反覆劇於前乎！

translations.literal: how can you now turn back and go to extremes worse than before!
translations.idiomatic: how can you now turn back and go to extremes worse than before!

sentences.zh: 「今民有七亡：陰陽不和，水旱為災，一亡也；

translations.literal: " Now the people have seven lacks: yin and yang not in harmony, flood and drought as disasters—the first lack;
translations.idiomatic: " Now the people suffer seven losses: yin and yang out of harmony and flood and drought—the first loss;

sentences.zh: 縣官重責，更賦租稅，二亡也；

translations.literal: the district offices impose heavy levies and repeatedly assess rent and tax—the second lack;
translations.idiomatic: district offices impose heavy levies and repeatedly assess rent and tax—the second loss;

sentences.zh: 貪吏並公，受取不已，三亡也；

translations.literal: greedy officials band together and take bribes without end—the third lack;
translations.idiomatic: greedy officials band together and take bribes without end—the third loss;

sentences.zh: 豪強大姓，蠶食亡厭，四亡也；

translations.literal: powerful clans and great surnames devour like silkworms without satiety—the fourth lack;
translations.idiomatic: powerful clans and great families devour without satiety—the fourth loss;

sentences.zh: 苛吏繇役，失農桑時，五亡也；

translations.literal: harsh officials and corvée labor cause loss of farming and sericulture seasons—the fifth lack;
translations.idiomatic: harsh officials and corvée labor cause the farming seasons to be missed—the fifth loss;

sentences.zh: 部落鼓鳴，男女遮列，六亡也；

translations.literal: in the hamlets drums sound and men and women block the roads in ranks—the sixth lack;
translations.idiomatic: in the hamlets drums sound and men and women block the roads—the sixth loss;

sentences.zh: 盜賊劫略，取民財物，七亡也。

translations.literal: bandits and robbers plunder and seize the people's goods—the seventh lack.
translations.idiomatic: bandits and robbers plunder the people's goods—the seventh loss.

sentences.zh: 七亡尚可，又有七死：酷吏毆殺，一死也；

translations.literal: The seven lacks can still be borne; there are also seven deaths: harsh officials beat and kill—the first death;
translations.idiomatic: The seven losses can still be borne; there are also seven deaths: harsh officials beat and kill—the first death;

sentences.zh: 治獄深刻，二死也；

translations.literal: handling prisons with severity and depth—the second death;
translations.idiomatic: handling prisons with severity—the second death;

sentences.zh: 冤陷亡辜，三死也；

translations.literal: wrongful imprisonment of the guiltless—the third death;
translations.idiomatic: wrongful imprisonment of the guiltless—the third death;

sentences.zh: 盜賊橫發，四死也；

translations.literal: bandits and robbers erupt across the land—the fourth death;
translations.idiomatic: bandits and robbers run rampant—the fourth death;

sentences.zh: 怨讎相殘，五死也；

translations.literal: enemies and foes mutually slaughter—the fifth death;
translations.idiomatic: enemies mutually slaughter—the fifth death;

sentences.zh: 歲惡飢餓，六死也；

translations.literal: years evil with famine and hunger—the sixth death;
translations.idiomatic: bad years with famine—the sixth death;

sentences.zh: 時氣疾疫，七死也。

translations.literal: seasonal qi and epidemic disease—the seventh death.
translations.idiomatic: seasonal epidemics—the seventh death.

sentences.zh: 民有七亡而無一得，慾望國安，誠難；

translations.literal: The people have seven lacks yet obtain not one; wishing the state's peace is truly hard;
translations.idiomatic: The people suffer seven losses yet gain not one; to wish the state secure is truly hard;

sentences.zh: 民有七死而無一生，慾望刑措，誠難。

translations.literal: the people have seven deaths yet not one life; wishing punishments set aside is truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: the people suffer seven deaths yet not one survives; to wish punishments set aside is truly hard.

sentences.zh: 此非公卿、守相貪殘成化之所致邪？

translations.literal: Is this not caused by the Three Dukes, governors, and chancellors—greedy and cruel—forming and transforming the age?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not caused by the greed and cruelty of the high ministers, governors, and chancellors shaping the age?

sentences.zh: 群臣幸得居尊官，食重祿，豈有肯加惻隱於細民，助陛下流教化者邪？

translations.literal: Your ministers are fortunate to hold honored offices and eat heavy salaries—how could there be any willing to add sympathetic pity toward the petty people and help Your Majesty spread transforming instruction?
translations.idiomatic: Your ministers are fortunate to hold high office and heavy salaries—would any add sympathy for the common people and help Your Majesty spread transforming instruction?

sentences.zh: 志但在營私家，稱賓客，為奸利而已。

translations.literal: Their intent is only to manage private households, praise retainers, and seek wicked profit.
translations.idiomatic: Their intent is only to manage private interests, praise retainers, and seek illicit profit.

sentences.zh: 以苟容曲從為賢，以拱默尸祿為智，謂如臣宣等為愚。

translations.literal: They take easy accommodation and crooked compliance as worthiness, take folded silence and corpse-like salaries as wisdom, and call men like your subject Xuan foolish.
translations.idiomatic: They take easy compliance as worthiness and folded silence while drawing salary as wisdom, and call men like your subject Xuan foolish.

sentences.zh: 陛下擢臣巖穴，誠翼有益豪毛，豈徒欲使臣美食大官、重高門之地哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty raised your subject from mountain caves; truly I hoped for benefit even to a hair's breadth—how could it be only to make your subject eat fine food, hold great offices, and weigh heavy gate estates!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty raised your subject from obscurity; I truly hoped to be of some use—even a hair's breadth of benefit—how could it be only to eat fine food, hold great office, and dwell in a grand estate!

sentences.zh: 「天下，乃皇天之天下也。

translations.literal: " All under Heaven is August Heaven's all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " All under Heaven belongs to August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 陛下上為皇天子，下為黎庶父母，為天牧養元元，視之當如一，合《尸鳩》之詩。

translations.literal: Your Majesty above is the August Son of Heaven, below are father and mother to the black-headed people; you pasture and nurture the primordial masses for Heaven and ought to view them as one—matching the Ode of the Pigeon.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty above is Son of Heaven, below father and mother to the people; you pasture the masses for Heaven and ought to view them as one—matching the Ode of the Pigeon.

sentences.zh: 今貧民菜食不厭，衣又穿空，父子、夫婦不能相保，誠可為酸鼻。

translations.literal: Now the poor eat vegetable food without being sated, clothes again are worn through with holes; father and son, husband and wife cannot preserve one another—truly it can make the nose sour.
translations.idiomatic: Now the poor eat vegetables without being sated and wear clothes worn through with holes; fathers and sons, husbands and wives cannot preserve one another—it is truly heartbreaking.

sentences.zh: 陛下不救，將安所歸命乎！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not rescue them, to where will they turn their lives!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not rescue them, to whom will they turn!

sentences.zh: 奈何獨私養外親與幸臣董賢，多賞賜，以大萬數，使奴從、賓客，漿酒藿肉，蒼頭廬兒，皆用致富，非天意也。

translations.literal: How can you alone privately nurture maternal kin and the favored minister Dong Xian, with many rewards and gifts by the tens of thousands, making slaves, followers, and retainers—with thin wine and bean-leaf meat, male slaves and hut boys—all use this to grow rich? It is not Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Why do you alone lavish private favor on maternal kin and the favored minister Dong Xian, rewarding them by the tens of thousands so that slaves, followers, and retainers—even with thin wine and bean-leaf meat, male slaves and hut boys—all grow rich? This is not Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 「及汝昌侯傅商，亡功而封。

translations.literal: " As for Marquis of Ruchang Fu Shang, without merit he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: " As for Marquis of Ruchang Fu Shang, he was enfeoffed without merit.

sentences.zh: 夫官爵非陛下之官爵，乃天下之官爵也。

translations.literal: For offices and ranks are not Your Majesty's offices and ranks—they are all under Heaven's offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: For offices and ranks are not Your Majesty's alone—they belong to all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 陛下取非其官，官非其人，而望天說民服，豈不難哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty takes offices that are not fitting, appoints offices to men who are not fitting, yet hopes Heaven is pleased and the people submit—is it not hard!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty bestows offices unfittingly and appoints unfit men, yet hopes Heaven will be pleased and the people submit—is that not hard!

sentences.zh: 方陽侯孫寵，宜陵侯息夫躬，辯足以移眾，強可用獨立，奸人之雄，惑世尤劇者也，宜以時罷退。

translations.literal: Marquis of Fangyang Sun Chong and Marquis of Yiling Xinfu Gong—eloquence enough to move the multitude, strength usable to stand alone, chiefs among wicked men, confusing the age with especial severity—ought in season to be dismissed and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Fangyang Sun Chong and Marquis of Yiling Xinfu Gong—eloquent enough to sway the multitude, strong enough to stand alone, chiefs among wicked men who confuse the age with especial severity—ought to be dismissed in season.

sentences.zh: 及外親幼童未通經術者，皆宜令休，就師傅。

translations.literal: And maternal kin who are young children not yet versed in the classics—all ought to be ordered to rest and go to teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Maternal kin who are young children not yet versed in the classics ought all to be sent home to their teachers.

sentences.zh: 急征故大司馬傅喜，使領外親。

translations.literal: Urgently summon the former Grand Marshal Fu Xi to make him lead the maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: Urgently summon former Grand Marshal Fu Xi to lead the maternal kin.

sentences.zh: 故大司空何武、師丹，故丞相孔光，故左將軍彭宣，經皆更博士，位皆歷三公；

translations.literal: Former Grand Minister of Works He Wu and Shi Dan, former Chancellor Kong Guang, former General of the Left Peng Xuan—all their classics were studied under erudites, all their posts reached the Three Dukes;
translations.idiomatic: Former Grand Minister of Works He Wu and Shi Dan, former Chancellor Kong Guang, former General of the Left Peng Xuan—all studied classics under erudites and all reached the Three Dukes;

sentences.zh: 龔勝為司直，郡國皆慎選舉；

translations.literal: Gong Sheng was Supervisor-Director and commanderies and states all carefully chose and promoted;
translations.idiomatic: Gong Sheng was Supervisor-Director and commanderies and states all chose officials carefully;

sentences.zh: 可大委任也。

translations.literal: they can be greatly entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: they can be greatly entrusted.

sentences.zh: 陛下前以小不忍退武等，海內失望。

translations.literal: Your Majesty earlier, for a small lack of forbearance, dismissed Wu and the others—all within the seas were disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty earlier dismissed Wu and the others for a small lack of forbearance, and all within the seas were disappointed.

sentences.zh: 陛下尚能容亡功德者甚眾，曾不能忍武等邪？

translations.literal: Your Majesty can still accommodate many without merit or virtue—could you not once bear Wu and the others?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty can still tolerate many without merit—could you not once bear Wu and the others?

sentences.zh: 治天下者，當用天下之心為心，不得自專快意而已也。

translations.literal: One who governs all under Heaven ought to use all under Heaven's heart as his heart and cannot merely follow his own exclusive pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: One who governs all under Heaven ought to take the heart of all under Heaven as his heart and cannot merely follow private pleasure.

sentences.zh: 」宣語雖刻切，上以宣名儒，優容之。

translations.literal: " Xuan's words though cutting were severe; the emperor because Xuan was a famed Confucian treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: " Though Xuan's words were cutting, the emperor, because Xuan was a famed Confucian, treated him with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 匈奴單于上書願朝五年。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu chanyu submitted a memorial wishing to attend court in the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu chanyu submitted a memorial wishing to attend court in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 時帝被疾，或言：「匈奴從上游來厭人；

translations.literal: At the time the emperor suffered illness; some said: "The Xiongnu coming from the upper reaches come to afflict people;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was ill; some said, "The Xiongnu coming from upstream bring affliction;

sentences.zh: 自黃龍、竟寧時，單于朝中國，輒有大故。

translations.literal: from the Huanglong and Jingning periods, whenever the chanyu attended the Middle Kingdom's court, there was always a great misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: since the Huanglong and Jingning periods, whenever the chanyu attended the Han court, some great misfortune followed.

sentences.zh: 」上由是難之，以問公卿，亦以為虛費府帑，可且勿許。

translations.literal: " The emperor therefore found it difficult and asked the Three Dukes; they also held it would waste the treasury empty and could for the time being not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor therefore hesitated and asked the high ministers; they also held it would waste the treasury and could for the time being be denied.

sentences.zh: 單于使辭去，未發，黃門郎揚雄上書諫曰：「臣聞《六經》之治，貴於未亂；

translations.literal: The chanyu's envoy took leave to depart and had not yet set out when Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Yang Xiong submitted a remonstrance, saying: "Your subject has heard that in governing by the Six Classics, what is prized is before disorder;
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu's envoy took leave to depart and had not yet set out when Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Yang Xiong memorialized in remonstrance, saying, "Your subject has heard that in governing by the Six Classics, what is prized is action before disorder;

sentences.zh: 兵家之勝，貴於未戰；

translations.literal: in the military family's victory, what is prized is before battle;
translations.idiomatic: in military victory, what is prized is triumph before battle;

sentences.zh: 二者皆微，然而大事之本，不可不察也。

translations.literal: both are subtle, yet they are the root of great affairs and cannot but be examined.
translations.idiomatic: both are subtle, yet they are the root of great affairs and cannot but be examined.

sentences.zh: 今單于上書求朝，國家不許而辭之，臣愚以為漢與匈奴從此隙矣。

translations.literal: Now the Chanyu has submitted a memorial requesting court audience, and the state has not permitted it but declined him; your servant is foolish and considers that Han and the Xiongnu from this will have a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Chanyu has submitted a memorial requesting an audience at court, and the state has refused and declined him; your servant is foolish enough to think that Han and the Xiongnu will from this have a rift.

sentences.zh: 匈奴本五帝所不能臣，三王所不能制，其不可使隙明甚。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu from the outset were what the Five Emperors could not make subjects and the Three Kings could not control—how clearly they must not be given a rift.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu from the outset were what the Five Emperors could not subdue and the Three Kings could not control—it is exceedingly clear that they must not be given cause for a rift.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢遠稱，請引秦以來明之：以秦始皇之強，蒙恬之威，然不敢窺西河，乃築長城以界之。

translations.literal: Your servant does not dare cite remote examples and asks to draw proof from Qin onward: with Qin Shihuang's strength and Meng Tian's might, yet they did not dare peer into the Western Bend and instead built the Long Wall to bound them.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant does not dare cite remote examples and asks to draw proof from Qin onward: with Qin Shihuang's strength and Meng Tian's might, they still did not dare encroach on the Western Bend and instead built the Long Wall to mark the boundary.

sentences.zh: 會漢初興，以高祖之威靈，三十萬眾困於平城，時奇譎之士、石畫之臣甚眾，卒其所以脫者，世莫得而言也。

translations.literal: It happened that when Han first rose, with Gaozu's majesty and spirit, three hundred thousand masses were trapped at Pingcheng; at the time crafty strategists and stone-tablet planners were very many, yet in the end how they escaped—generations have not been able to say.
translations.idiomatic: When Han first rose, with Gaozu's majesty, three hundred thousand men were trapped at Pingcheng; crafty strategists and master planners were plentiful, yet how they escaped in the end—no generation has been able to say.

sentences.zh: 又高皇后時，匈奴悖慢，大臣權書遺之，然後得解。

translations.literal: Again in Empress Dowager Gao's time the Xiongnu were insolent and slow; a great minister by forged letter sent it to them, and only then was there release.
translations.idiomatic: Again in Empress Dowager Gao's time the Xiongnu were insolent; a great minister sent them a forged letter, and only then was there relief.

sentences.zh: 及孝文時，匈奴侵暴北邊，候騎至雍甘泉，京師大駭，發三將軍屯細柳、棘門、霸上以備之，數月乃罷。

translations.literal: By Emperor Wen's time the Xiongnu invaded and ravaged the northern frontier; scout horsemen reached Yong and Ganquan, and the capital was greatly alarmed; three generals were dispatched to garrison at Xiliu, Jimen, and Bashang to guard against them—only after several months was it ended.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Wen's time the Xiongnu raided the northern frontier; scout horsemen reached Yong and Ganquan, and the capital was greatly alarmed; three generals were posted at Xiliu, Jimen, and Bashang to guard against them—only after several months was the emergency ended.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，設馬邑之權，欲誘匈奴，徒費財勞師，一虜不可得見，況單于之面乎！

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne he set the Mayi stratagem, wishing to lure the Xiongnu—only to waste wealth and weary the army; not one captive could be obtained to see, how much less the Chanyu's face!
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne he set the Mayi stratagem to lure the Xiongnu—only to waste wealth and weary the army; not one captive could be taken, how much less the Chanyu's face!

sentences.zh: 其後深惟社稷之計，規恢萬載之策，乃大興師數十萬，使衛青、霍去病操兵，前後十餘年，於是浮西河，絕大幕，破寘顏，襲王庭，窮極其地，追奔逐北，封狼居胥山，禪於姑衍，以臨翰海，虜名王、貴人以百數。

translations.literal: Afterward he deeply weighed the altars of state, planned policies to restore ten thousand generations, and thereupon greatly raised armies of several hundred thousand, making Wei Qing and Huo Qubing wield troops—for more than ten years before and after—thus crossing the Western Bend, cutting through the Great Desert, breaking Zhizhi, striking the royal court, exhausting their lands, pursuing the fleeing and driving north, feng-shan at Mount Langjuxu, chan at Guyan, overlooking Hanhai, and capturing several hundred of their famous kings and nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he deeply weighed the state's welfare and planned policies for ten thousand generations, and thereupon raised armies of several hundred thousand, putting Wei Qing and Huo Qubing in command of troops—for more than ten years—crossing the Western Bend, cutting through the great desert, defeating Zhizhi, striking the royal court, exhausting their lands, pursuing the fleeing and driving them north, performing feng at Mount Langjuxu and chan at Guyan, overlooking Hanhai, and capturing several hundred of their famous kings and nobles.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，匈奴震怖，益求和親，然而未肯稱臣也。

translations.literal: From this afterward the Xiongnu were shaken and terrified and increasingly sought peace marriage, yet they were still unwilling to call themselves subjects.
translations.idiomatic: From this onward the Xiongnu were shaken and terrified and increasingly sought peace marriages, yet they still would not call themselves subjects.

sentences.zh: 且夫前世豈樂傾無量之費，役無罪之人，快心狼望之北哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, did former ages delight in pouring out measureless expense and conscripting guiltless people to gratify their hearts on the wolf-gazing north?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, did former ages delight in pouring out measureless expense and conscripting innocent people to gratify their hearts on the wolf-gazing north?

sentences.zh: 以為不壹勞者不久佚，不暫費者不永寧，是以忍百萬之師以摧餓虎之喙，運府庫之財填盧山之壑而不悔也。

translations.literal: They considered that one who does not endure labor once will not long enjoy ease, and one who does not spend briefly will not forever be secure; therefore they bore armies of a million to break the starving tiger's beak and moved treasury wealth to fill Lushan's ravines without regret.
translations.idiomatic: They held that one who does not endure labor once will not long enjoy ease, and one who does not spend briefly will not be secure forever; therefore they bore armies of a million to break the starving tiger's jaw and moved treasury wealth to fill Lushan's ravines without regret.

sentences.zh: 至本始之初，匈奴有桀心，欲掠烏孫，侵公主，乃發五將之師十五萬騎以擊之，時鮮有所獲，徒奮揚威武，明漢兵若雷風耳！

translations.literal: By the opening of Benji the Xiongnu had a fierce heart, wished to plunder the Wusun and encroach on the princess, and therefore five generals' hosts of one hundred fifty thousand horsemen were raised to strike them—at the time little was captured; they only roused and displayed might and majesty, clarifying that Han troops were like thunder and wind!
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Benji era the Xiongnu grew fierce, wished to plunder the Wusun and encroach on the princess, and therefore hosts of five generals and one hundred fifty thousand horsemen were raised to strike them—little was captured at the time; they only displayed might and majesty, making clear that Han troops were like thunder and wind!

sentences.zh: 雖空行空反，尚誅兩將軍，故北狄不服，中國未得高枕安寢也。

translations.literal: Though they marched out empty and returned empty, two generals were still executed; therefore the northern Di did not submit and the Central States could not pillow their heads high and sleep in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Though they marched out empty and returned empty, two generals were still executed; therefore the northern barbarians did not submit and the Central States could not sleep in peace.

sentences.zh: 逮至元康、神爵之間，大化神明，鴻恩溥洽，而匈奴內亂，五單于爭立，日逐、呼韓邪攜國歸死，扶伏稱臣，然尚羈縻之，計不顓制。

translations.literal: Down to between Yuankang and Shenjue, great transformation was divine and bright, vast grace broadly harmonized, while the Xiongnu were in internal disorder—five chanyus contended for the throne; Rizhu and Huhanye brought their states to submit to death, prostrating themselves and calling themselves subjects, yet they were still held by bridling reins and the plan was not to control them exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the Yuankang and Shenjue eras, great transformation was divine and bright and vast grace broadly harmonized, while the Xiongnu fell into internal disorder—five chanyus contended for the throne; Rizhu and Huhanye brought their states to submit, prostrating themselves and calling themselves subjects, yet they were still held on loose reins and the plan was not to control them exclusively.

sentences.zh: 自此之後，欲朝者不距，不欲者不強。

translations.literal: From this afterward, those who wished to attend court were not rejected; those who did not wish were not compelled.
translations.idiomatic: From this onward, those who wished to attend court were not rejected; those who did not wish were not compelled.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 外國天性忿鷙，形容魁健，負力怙氣，難化以善，易肄以惡，其強難詘，其和難得。

translations.literal: Foreign states by nature are fierce and proud, in form tall and strong, relying on strength and trusting in spirit—hard to transform with goodness, easy to indulge in evil; their strength is hard to bend and their harmony hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign states by nature are fierce and proud, tall and strong in form, relying on strength and trusting in spirit—hard to transform with goodness, easy to indulge in evil; their strength is hard to bend and their harmony hard to obtain.

sentences.zh: 故未服之時，勞師遠攻，傾國殫貨，伏屍流血，破堅拔敵，如彼之難也；

translations.literal: Therefore when not yet submitted, to weary the army in distant attack, exhaust the state and spend all goods, lie corpses and shed blood, break strongholds and pluck out the enemy—was as difficult as that;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when they had not yet submitted, to weary the army in distant attack, exhaust the state and spend all goods, lie corpses and shed blood, and break strongholds and rout the enemy—was as difficult as that;

sentences.zh: 既服之後，慰薦撫循，交接賂遺，威儀俯仰，如此之備也。

translations.literal: once submitted, to comfort, recommend, soothe, and tend them, exchange gifts and presents, and adjust ceremony high and low—was as complete as this.
translations.idiomatic: once they had submitted, to comfort, recommend, soothe, and tend them, exchange gifts and presents, and adjust ceremony high and low—was as complete as this.

sentences.zh: 往時嘗屠大宛之城，蹈烏桓之壘，探姑繒之壁，藉蕩姐之場，艾朝鮮之旃，拔兩越之旗，近不過旬月之役，遠不離二時之勞，固已犁其庭，掃其閭，郡縣而置之，雲徹席捲，後無餘災。

translations.literal: In former times they once slaughtered Dayuan's city, trampled the Wuhuan's ramparts, probed the Gungzang's walls, tread the Dangjie's ground, cut Korea's banners, and plucked the Two Yues' flags—near campaigns did not exceed a ten-day month's service, far ones did not depart from two seasons' labor; they had already plowed their courts, swept their lanes, set them as commanderies and counties, clouds penetrating and mats rolling up, with no aftermath disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In former times they once slaughtered Dayuan's city, trampled the Wuhuan's ramparts, probed the Gungzang's walls, tread the Dangjie's ground, cut down Korea's banners, and plucked the Two Yues' flags—near campaigns did not exceed a month's service, far ones no more than two seasons' labor; they had already plowed their courts, swept their lanes, established commanderies and counties, swept through like clouds rolling up mats, with no lingering disaster.

sentences.zh: 唯北狄為不然，真中國之堅敵也，三垂比之縣矣；

translations.literal: Only the northern Di were not so—truly the Central States' firm enemy; the three frontiers compared to them are as if suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Only the northern Di were not so—truly the Central States' stubborn enemy; the three frontiers compared to them are worlds apart;

sentences.zh: 前世重之茲甚，未易可輕也。

translations.literal: former ages esteemed them this greatly—they are not easily to be taken lightly.
translations.idiomatic: former ages esteemed them this greatly—they cannot easily be taken lightly.

sentences.zh: 「今單于歸義，懷款誠之心，欲離其庭，陳見於前，此乃上世之遺策，神靈之所想望，國家雖費，不得已者也。

translations.literal: " Now the Chanyu returns to righteousness, harbors sincere and earnest heart, wishes to leave his court and present himself before us—this is a legacy stratagem of higher ages and what spirits and numina yearn toward; though the state spends, it is what cannot be avoided."
translations.idiomatic: " Now the Chanyu returns to righteousness, harbors a sincere and earnest heart, wishes to leave his court and present himself before us—this is a legacy stratagem of higher ages and what spirits yearn toward; though the state must spend, it is unavoidable."

sentences.zh: 奈何距以來厭之辭，疏以無日之期，消往昔之恩，開將來之隙？

translations.literal: How can we reject him with words that weary his coming, distance him with a date that has no day, dissolve former grace, and open a rift for the future?
translations.idiomatic: How can we reject him with words that weary his coming, distance him with a date that has no fixed day, dissolve former grace, and open a rift for the future?

sentences.zh: 夫疑而隙之，使有恨心，負前言，緣往辭，歸怨於漢，因以自絕，終無北面之心，威之不可，諭之不能，焉得不為大憂乎！

translations.literal: To doubt him and rift with him will make him bear a resentful heart, go against former words, follow past declarations, return blame upon Han, and thereby cut himself off—in the end having no heart to face north; prestige cannot awe him, persuasion cannot instruct him—how can one not make this a great worry!
translations.idiomatic: To doubt him and create a rift will make him bear resentment, go against former words, follow past declarations, and return blame upon Han, thereby cutting himself off—in the end having no heart to face north; prestige cannot awe him and persuasion cannot instruct him—how can this not be a great worry!

sentences.zh: 夫明者視於無形，聰者聽於無聲，誠先於未然，即兵革不用而憂患不生。

translations.literal: The clear-sighted see in what has no form; the keen-eared hear in what has no sound; sincerity precedes what is not yet—then weapons and armor are not used and worry and disaster do not arise.
translations.idiomatic: The clear-sighted see what has no form; the keen-eared hear what has no sound; sincerity precedes what is not yet—then arms are not used and calamity does not arise.

sentences.zh: 不然，壹有隙之後，雖智者勞心於內，辯者轂擊於外，猶不若未然之時也。

translations.literal: If not so, once there is a rift, though the wise toil in mind within and debaters clash wheels without, it is still not like the time before it was so.
translations.idiomatic: If not so, once there is a rift, though the wise toil in mind within and debaters clash wheels without, it is still not like the time before it happened.

sentences.zh: 且往者圖西域，制車師，置城郭都護三十六國，費歲以大萬計者，豈為康居、烏孫能逾白龍堆而寇西邊哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, in former times they plotted the Western Regions, controlled the Cheshi, and established the garrison commandant over thirty-six walled states—expense yearly in the tens of thousands—was it because Kangju and Wusun could cross the White Dragon Mounds and raid the western frontier?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in former times they plotted the Western Regions, controlled Cheshi, and established the garrison commandant over thirty-six walled states at yearly expense in the tens of thousands—was it because Kangju and Wusun could cross the White Dragon Mounds and raid the western frontier?

sentences.zh: 乃以制匈奴也。

translations.literal: It was to control the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: It was to control the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 夫百年勞之，一日失之，費十而愛一，臣竊為國不安也。

translations.literal: A hundred years' labor—lost in a day; spending ten yet cherishing one—your servant privately considers the state insecure.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred years' labor—lost in a day; spending ten yet cherishing one—your servant privately considers the state insecure.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下少留意於未亂、未戰，以遏邊萌之禍！

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty give a little heed to before disorder and before battle, to check the disaster of frontier sprouts!"
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty give a little heed to before disorder and before battle, to check the disaster of frontier sprouts!"

sentences.zh: 書奏，天子寤焉，召還匈奴使者，更報單于書而許之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Son of Heaven awoke to it, recalled the Xiongnu envoy, and again replied to the Chanyu's letter, permitting him.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor awoke to it, recalled the Xiongnu envoy, and again replied to the Chanyu's letter, granting permission.

sentences.zh: 賜雄帛五十匹，黃金十斤。

translations.literal: Xiong was granted fifty bolts of silk and ten catties of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong was granted fifty bolts of silk and ten catties of gold.

sentences.zh: 單于未發，會病，復遣使願朝明年；

translations.literal: The Chanyu had not yet set out when he fell ill; he again sent an envoy wishing to attend court next year;
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu had not yet set out when he fell ill; he again sent an envoy wishing to attend court the following year;

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor permitted it.

sentences.zh: 董賢貴幸日盛，丁、傅害其寵，孔鄉侯晏與息夫躬謀欲求居位輔政。

translations.literal: Dong Xian's honored favor grew daily; the Ding and Fu clans resented his favor; Marquis of Kongxiang Yan and Yifu Gong plotted, wishing to obtain position and assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xian's favored status grew daily; the Ding and Fu clans resented his favor; Marquis of Kongxiang Yan and Yifu Gong plotted, wishing to obtain position and assist in government.

sentences.zh: 會單于以病未朝，躬因是而上奏，以為：「單于當以十一月入塞，後以病為解，疑有他變。

translations.literal: It happened that because the Chanyu was ill and did not attend court, Gong took occasion to submit a memorial, holding: "The Chanyu ought to have entered the passes in the eleventh month; afterward he used illness as excuse—your servant suspects there is some other change.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that because the Chanyu was ill and did not attend court, Gong took occasion to submit a memorial, holding, "The Chanyu ought to have entered the passes in the eleventh month; afterward he used illness as an excuse—your servant suspects there is some other change.

sentences.zh: 烏孫兩昆彌弱，卑爰疐強盛，東結單于，遣子往侍，恐其合勢以並烏孫；

translations.literal: The Wusun's two kunmis are weak; Beizhi Que is strong and flourishing, has allied east with the Chanyu, and sent his son to attend in service—your servant fears they will combine strength to annex the Wusun;
translations.idiomatic: The Wusun's two kunmis are weak; Beizhi Que is strong and flourishing, has allied east with the Chanyu, and sent his son to attend in service—your servant fears they will combine strength to annex the Wusun;

sentences.zh: 烏孫並，則匈奴盛而西域危矣。

translations.literal: if the Wusun are annexed, then the Xiongnu will flourish and the Western Regions will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: if the Wusun are annexed, then the Xiongnu will flourish and the Western Regions will be in peril.

sentences.zh: 可令降胡詐為卑爰疐使者來上書，欲因天子威告單于歸臣侍子，因下其章，令匈奴客聞焉；

translations.literal: One may order surrendered Hu to feign being Beizhi Que's envoy to come submit a memorial, wishing to use the Son of Heaven's prestige to tell the Chanyu to return his subject and attending son; thereby send down his memorial and let Xiongnu guests hear it;
translations.idiomatic: One may order surrendered Hu to feign being Beizhi Que's envoy and submit a memorial, wishing to use the Son of Heaven's prestige to tell the Chanyu to return his subject and attending son; thereby send down his memorial and let Xiongnu guests hear it;

sentences.zh: 則是所謂『上兵伐謀，其次伐交』者也。

translations.literal: then this is what is called 'the highest military art attacks stratagems; next, attacks alliances.'"
translations.idiomatic: then this is what is called 'the highest military art attacks stratagems; next, attacks alliances.'"

sentences.zh: 」書奏，上引見躬，召公卿、將軍大議。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor summoned Gong for audience, called the excellencies, ministers, and generals to great deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor summoned Gong for audience and called the excellencies, ministers, and generals to great deliberation.

sentences.zh: 左將軍公孫祿以為：「中國常以威信懷伏夷狄，躬欲逆詐，進不信之謀，不可許。

translations.literal: Left General Gongsun Lu held: "The Central States constantly use authority and prestige to embrace and subdue the Yi and Di; Gong wishes to go against and deceive, advancing untrustworthy stratagems—it cannot be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Left General Gongsun Lu held, "The Central States constantly use authority and prestige to embrace and subdue the Yi and Di; Gong wishes to resort to deception and advance untrustworthy stratagems—it cannot be permitted.

sentences.zh: 且匈奴賴先帝之德，保塞稱蕃。

translations.literal: Moreover the Xiongnu rely on the former emperor's virtue, guard the passes, and style themselves vassals.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Xiongnu rely on the former emperor's virtue, guard the passes, and style themselves vassals.

sentences.zh: 今單于以疾病不任奉朝賀，遣使自陳，不失臣子之禮。

translations.literal: Now the Chanyu, because of illness, cannot bear to perform court congratulations, and sent an envoy to state it himself—he has not lost the rites of minister and son.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Chanyu, because of illness, cannot perform court congratulations and sent an envoy to state it himself—he has not lost the rites of minister and son.

sentences.zh: 臣祿自保沒身不見匈奴為邊竟憂也！

translations.literal: Your servant Lu personally guarantees that to the end of his life he will not see the Xiongnu become a worry for the frontier borders!"
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Lu personally guarantees that in his lifetime he will not see the Xiongnu become a worry for the frontier borders!"

sentences.zh: 」躬掎祿曰：「臣為國家計，冀先謀將然，豫圖未形，為萬世慮。

translations.literal: " Gong seized Lu and said: "Your servant plans for the state, hoping to plot first what will be so, to map beforehand what has no form, and to calculate for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: " Gong seized Lu and said, "Your servant plans for the state, hoping to plot first what will be so, to map beforehand what has no form, and to calculate for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 而祿欲以其犬馬齒保目所見。

translations.literal: Yet Lu wishes with his dog-and-horse years to guarantee only what his eyes have seen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lu wishes with his remaining years to guarantee only what his eyes have seen.

sentences.zh: 臣與祿異議，未可同日語也！

translations.literal: Your servant and Lu hold different views—they cannot be spoken of on the same day!"
translations.idiomatic: Your servant and Lu hold different views—they cannot be spoken of on the same day!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「善！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Good!"

sentences.zh: 」乃罷群臣，獨與躬議。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he dismissed the assembled ministers and deliberated with Gong alone.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he dismissed the assembled ministers and deliberated with Gong alone.

sentences.zh: 躬因建言：「災異屢見，恐必有非常之變，可遣大將軍行邊兵，敕武備，斬一郡守以立威，震四夷，因以厭應變異。

translations.literal: Gong thereupon offered counsel: "Strange disasters have repeatedly appeared—your servant fears there must be an extraordinary change; one may dispatch the Grand General to march the frontier troops, order martial readiness, behead one commandery administrator to establish prestige, shake the four Yi, and thereby respond to and satisfy the strange disasters."
translations.idiomatic: Gong thereupon offered counsel, "Strange disasters have repeatedly appeared—your servant fears there must be an extraordinary change; one may dispatch the Grand General to march the frontier troops, order martial readiness, behead one commandery administrator to establish prestige, shake the four barbarians, and thereby respond to the strange disasters."

sentences.zh: 」上然之，以問丞相嘉，對曰：「臣聞動民以行不以言，應天以實不以文。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved it and questioned Chancellor Jia; he replied: "Your servant has heard that one moves the people by conduct, not by words, and responds to Heaven by substance, not by ornament.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved it and questioned Chancellor Jia; he replied, "Your servant has heard that one moves the people by conduct, not by words, and responds to Heaven by substance, not by ornament.

sentences.zh: 下民微細，猶不可詐，況於上天神明而可欺哉！

translations.literal: The lower people are minute and fine—even they cannot be deceived; how much less the supreme Heaven's numinous clarity—can it be deceived!
translations.idiomatic: The lower people are minute and fine—even they cannot be deceived; how much less supreme Heaven's numinous clarity—can it be deceived!

sentences.zh: 天之見異，所以敕戒人君，欲令覺悟反正，推誠行善，民心說而天意得矣！

translations.literal: Heaven's appearance of strangeness is to admonish and warn the human ruler, wishing to make him awaken, turn back, extend sincerity and practice goodness—then the people's hearts are pleased and Heaven's intent is obtained!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's appearance of strangeness is to admonish and warn the ruler, wishing to make him awaken, turn back, extend sincerity and practice goodness—then the people's hearts are pleased and Heaven's intent is obtained!

sentences.zh: 辯士見一端，或妄以意傅著星歷，虛造匈奴、烏孫、西羌之難，謀動干戈，設為權變，非應天之道也。

translations.literal: Debaters see one end and perhaps recklessly by intent attach it to star calendars, falsely fabricating difficulties of the Xiongnu, Wusun, and Western Qiang, plotting to move weapons and armor and set up expedient changes—this is not the Way of responding to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Debaters see one end and perhaps recklessly attach it to star calendars, falsely fabricating difficulties of the Xiongnu, Wusun, and Western Qiang, plotting to move arms and set up expedient changes—this is not the Way of responding to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 守相有罪，車馳詣闕，交臂就死，恐懼如此，而談說者欲動安之危，辯口快耳，其實未可從。

translations.literal: When administrators and chancellors have offense, chariots race to the palace gates and they fold arms to accept death—fear is like this; yet those who talk and persuade wish to move what is settled into danger, quick tongues for the ear—in substance it cannot be followed.
translations.idiomatic: When administrators and chancellors have offense, chariots race to the palace gates and they fold arms to accept death—fear is like this; yet those who talk and persuade wish to move what is settled into danger, quick tongues for the ear—in substance it cannot be followed.

sentences.zh: 夫議政者，苦其諂諛、傾險、辯惠、深刻也。

translations.literal: Those who deliberate on government suffer from flattery, perverse danger, eloquent cleverness, and cutting depth.
translations.idiomatic: Those who deliberate on government suffer from flattery, perverse danger, eloquent cleverness, and cutting depth.

sentences.zh: 昔秦繆公不從百里奚、蹇叔之言，以敗其師，其悔過自責，疾詿誤之臣，思黃發之言，名垂於後世。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Mu of Qin did not follow the words of Baili Xi and Jian Shu and thereby defeated his army; he repented, blamed himself, hated misleading ministers, and thought on words of gray hair—his name hangs down to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Mu of Qin did not follow the words of Baili Xi and Jian Shu and thereby defeated his army; he repented, blamed himself, hated misleading ministers, and heeded words of gray hair—his name hangs down to later ages.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下觀覽古戒，反覆參考，無以先入之語為主！

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty survey ancient warnings, turn and again compare and consult, and not take words that came first as master!"
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty survey ancient warnings, turn and again compare and consult, and not take words that came first as master!"

sentences.zh: 」上不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not heed it.
